text: of Syria, and of Moab, and of the children of Ammon, and of the Philistines, and of Amalek, and of the spoil of Hadadezer, son of Rehob, king of Zobah.

title: 2 Samuel 8:13
text: David earned a reputation when he returned from smiting the Syrians in the Valley of Salt, even eighteen thousand men.

title: 2 Samuel 8:14
text: He put garrisons in Edom; throughout all Edom put he garrisons, and all the Edomites became servants to David. Yahweh gave victory to David wherever he went.

title: 2 Samuel 8:15
text: David reigned over all Israel; and David executed justice and righteousness to all his people.

title: 2 Samuel 8:16
text: Joab the son of Zeruiah was over the army; and Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud was recorder;

title: 2 Samuel 8:17
text: and Zadok the son of Ahitub, and Ahimelech the son of Abiathar, were priests; and Seraiah was scribe;

title: 2 Samuel 8:18
text: and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada [was over] the Cherethites and the Pelethites; and David's sons were chief ministers.

title: 2 Samuel 9:1
text: David said, "Is there yet any who is left of the house of Saul, that I may show him kindness for Jonathan's sake?"

title: 2 Samuel 9:2
text: There was of the house of Saul a servant whose name was Ziba, and they called him to David; and the king said to him, "Are you Ziba?" He said, "Your servant is he."

title: 2 Samuel 9:3
text: The king said, "Is there not yet any of the house of Saul, that I may show the kindness of God to him?" Ziba said to the king, "Jonathan has yet a son, who is lame of his feet."

title: 2 Samuel 9:4
text: The king said to him, "Where is he?" Ziba said to the king, "Behold, he is in the house of Machir the son of Ammiel, in Lo Debar."

title: 2 Samuel 9:5
text: Then king David sent, and fetched him out of the house of Machir the son of Ammiel, from Lo Debar.

title: 2 Samuel 9:6
text: Mephibosheth, the son of Jonathan, the son of Saul, came to David, and fell on his face, and did obeisance. David said, "Mephibosheth." He answered, "Behold, your servant!"

title: 2 Samuel 9:7
text: David said to him, "Don't be afraid of him; for I will surely show you kindness for Jonathan your father's sake, and will restore to you all the land of Saul your father. You shall eat bread at my table continually."

title: 2 Samuel 9:8
text: He did obeisance, and said, "What is your servant, that you should look on such a dead dog as I am?"

title: 2 Samuel 9:9
text: Then the king called to Ziba, Saul's servant, and said to him, "All that pertained to Saul and to all his house have I given to your master's son.

title: 2 Samuel 9:10
text: You shall till the land for him, you, and your sons, and your servants; and you shall bring in [the fruits], that your master's son may have bread to eat: but Mephibosheth your master's son shall eat bread always at my table." Now Ziba had fifteen sons and twenty servants.

title: 2 Samuel 9:11
text: Then Ziba said to the king, "According to all that my lord the king commands his servant, so your shall servant do." So Mephibosheth ate at the king's table, like one of the king's sons.

title: 2 Samuel 9:12
text: Mephibosheth had a young son, whose name was Mica. All that lived in the house of Ziba were servants to Mephibosheth.

title: 2 Samuel 9:13
text: So Mephibosheth lived in Jerusalem; for he ate continually at the king's table. He was lame in both his feet.

title: 2 Samuel 10:1
text: It happened after this, that the king of the children of Ammon died, and Hanun his son reigned in his place.

title: 2 Samuel 10:2
text: David said, "I will show kindness to Hanun the son of Nahash, as his father showed kindness to me." So David sent by his servants to comfort him concerning his father. David's servants came into the land of the children of Ammon.

title: 2 Samuel 10:3
text: But the princes of the children of Ammon said to Hanun their lord, "Do you think that David honors your father, in that he has sent comforters to you? Hasn't David sent his servants to you to search the city, and to spy it out, and to overthrow it?"

title: 2 Samuel 10:4
text: So Hanun took David's servants, and shaved off the one half of their beards, and cut off their garments in the middle, even to their buttocks, and sent them away.

title: 2 Samuel 10:5
text: When they told it to David, he sent to meet them; for the men were greatly ashamed. The king said, "Wait at Jericho until your beards have grown, and then return."

title: 2 Samuel 10:6
text: When the children of Ammon saw that they were become odious to David, the children of Ammon sent and hired the Syrians of Beth Rehob, and the Syrians of Zobah, twenty thousand footmen, and the king of Maacah with one thousand men, and the men of Tob twelve thousand men.

title: 2 Samuel 10:7
text: When David heard of it, he sent Joab, and all the army of the mighty men.

title: 2 Samuel 10:8
text: The children of Ammon came out, and put the battle in array at the entrance of the gate: and the Syrians of Zobah and of Rehob, and the men of Tob and Maacah, were by themselves in the field.

title: 2 Samuel 10:9
text: Now when Joab saw that the battle was set against him before and behind, he chose of all the choice men of Israel, and put them in array against the Syrians:

title: 2 Samuel 10:10
text: The rest of the people he committed into the hand of Abishai his brother; and he put them in array against the children of Ammon.

title: 2 Samuel 10:11
text: He said, "If the Syrians are too strong for me, then you shall help me; but if the children of Ammon are too strong for you, then I will come and help you.

title: 2 Samuel 10:12
text: Be courageous, and let us be strong for our people, and for the cities of our God; and Yahweh do that which seems good to him."

title: 2 Samuel 10:13
text: So Joab and the people who were with him drew near to the battle against the Syrians: and they fled before him.

title: 2 Samuel 10:14
text: When the children of Ammon saw that the Syrians had fled, they likewise fled before Abishai, and entered into the city. Then Joab returned from the children of Ammon, and came to Jerusalem.

title: 2 Samuel 10:15
text: When the Syrians saw that they were defeated by Israel, they gathered themselves together.

title: 2 Samuel 10:16
text: Hadadezer sent, and brought out the Syrians who were beyond the River: and they came to Helam, with Shobach the captain of the army of Hadadezer at their head.

title: 2 Samuel 10:17
text: It was told David; and he gathered all Israel together, and passed over the Jordan, and came to Helam. The Syrians set themselves in array against David, and fought with him.

title: 2 Samuel 10:18
text: The Syrians fled before Israel; and David killed of the Syrians [the men of] seven hundred chariots, and forty thousand horsemen, and struck Shobach the captain of their army, so that he died there.

title: 2 Samuel 10:19
text: When all the kings who were servants to Hadadezer saw that they were defeated before Israel, they made peace with Israel, and served them. So the Syrians feared to help the children of Ammon any more.

title: 2 Samuel 11:1
text: It happened, at the return of the year, at the time when kings go out [to battle], that David sent Joab, and his servants with him, and all Israel; and they destroyed the children of Ammon, and besieged Rabbah. But David stayed at Jerusalem.

title: 2 Samuel 11:2
text: It happened at evening, that David arose from off his bed, and walked on the roof of the king's house: and from the roof he saw a woman bathing; and the woman was very beautiful to look on.

title: 2 Samuel 11:3
text: David sent and inquired after the woman. One said, "Isn't this Bathsheba, the daughter of Eliam, the wife of Uriah the Hittite?"

title: 2 Samuel 11:4
text: David sent messengers, and took her; and she came in to him, and he lay with her (for she was purified from her uncleanness); and she returned to her house.

title: 2 Samuel 11:5
text: The woman conceived; and she sent and told David, and said, "I am with child."

title: 2 Samuel 11:6
text: David sent to Joab, [saying], "Send me Uriah the Hittite." Joab sent Uriah to David.

title: 2 Samuel 11:7
text: When Uriah was come to him, David asked of him how Joab did, and how the people fared, and how the war prospered.

title: 2 Samuel 11:8
text: David said to Uriah, "Go down to your house, and wash your feet." Uriah departed out of the king's house, and a gift from the king was sent after him.

title: 2 Samuel 11:9
text: But Uriah slept at the door of the king's house with all the servants of his lord, and didn't go down to his house.

title: 2 Samuel 11:10
text: When they had told David, saying, "Uriah didn't go down to his house," David said to Uriah, "Haven't you come from a journey? Why didn't you go down to your house?"

title: 2 Samuel 11:11
text: Uriah said to David, "The ark, Israel, and Judah, are staying in tents; and my lord Joab, and the servants of my lord, are encamped in the open field. Shall I then go into my house to eat and to drink, and to lie with my wife? As you live, and as your soul lives, I will not do this thing!"

title: 2 Samuel 11:12
text: David said to Uriah, "Stay here today also, and tomorrow I will let you depart." So Uriah stayed in Jerusalem that day, and the next day.

title: 2 Samuel 11:13
text: When David had called him, he ate and drink before him; and he made him drunk. At evening, he went out to lie on his bed with the servants of his lord, but didn't go down to his house.

title: 2 Samuel 11:14
text: It happened in the morning, that David wrote a letter to Joab, and sent it by the hand of Uriah.

title: 2 Samuel 11:15
text: He wrote in the letter, saying, "Send Uriah to the forefront of the hottest battle, and retreat from him, that he may be struck, and die."

title: 2 Samuel 11:16
text: It happened, when Joab kept watch on the city, that he assigned Uriah to the place where he knew that valiant men were.

title: 2 Samuel 11:17
text: The men of the city went out, and fought with Joab. Some of the people fell, even of the servants of David; and Uriah the Hittite died also.

title: 2 Samuel 11:18
text: Then Joab sent and told David all the things concerning the war;

title: 2 Samuel 11:19
text: and he commanded the messenger, saying, "When you have finished telling all the things concerning the war to the king,

title: 2 Samuel 11:20
text: it shall be that, if the king's wrath arise, and he asks you, 'Why did you go so near to the city to fight? Didn't you know that they would shoot from the wall?

title: 2 Samuel 11:21
text: who struck Abimelech the son of Jerubbesheth? Didn't a woman cast an upper millstone on him from the wall, so that he died at Thebez? Why did you go so near the wall?' then you shall say, 'Your servant Uriah the Hittite is dead also.'"

title: 2 Samuel 11:22
text: So the messenger went, and came and showed David all that Joab had sent him for.

title: 2 Samuel 11:23
text: The messenger said to David, "The men prevailed against us, and came out to us into the field, and we were on them even to the entrance of the gate.

title: 2 Samuel 11:24
text: The shooters shot at your servants from off the wall; and some of the king's servants are dead, and your servant Uriah the Hittite is dead also."

title: 2 Samuel 11:25
text: Then David said to the messenger, "Thus you shall tell Joab, 'Don't let this thing displease you, for the sword devours one as well as another. Make your battle stronger against the city, and overthrow it.' Encourage him."

title: 2 Samuel 11:26
text: When the wife of Uriah heard that Uriah her husband was dead, she made lamentation for her husband.

title: 2 Samuel 11:27
text: When the mourning was past, David sent and took her home to his house, and she became his wife, and bore him a son. But the thing that David had done displeased Yahweh.

title: 2 Samuel 12:1
text: Yahweh sent Nathan to David. He came to him, and said to him, "There were two men in one city; the one rich, and the other poor.

title: 2 Samuel 12:2
text: The rich man had very many flocks and herds,

title: 2 Samuel 12:3
text: but the poor man had nothing, except one little ewe lamb, which he had bought and raised. It grew up together with him, and with his children. It ate of his own food, drank of his own cup, and lay in his bosom, and was to him like a daughter.

title: 2 Samuel 12:4
text: A traveler came to the rich man, and he spared to take of his own flock and of his own herd, to dress for the wayfaring man who had come to him, but took the poor man's lamb, and dressed it for the man who had come to him."

title: 2 Samuel 12:5
text: David's anger was greatly kindled against the man, and he said to Nathan, "As Yahweh lives, the man who has done this is worthy to die!

title: 2 Samuel 12:6
text: He shall restore the lamb fourfold, because he did this thing, and because he had no pity!"

title: 2 Samuel 12:7
text: Nathan said to David, "You are the man. This is what Yahweh, the God of Israel, says: 'I anointed you king over Israel, and I delivered you out of the hand of Saul.

title: 2 Samuel 12:8
text: I gave you your master's house, and your master's wives into your bosom, and gave you the house of Israel and of Judah; and if that would have been too little, I would have added to you many more such things.

title: 2 Samuel 12:9
text: Why have you despised the word of Yahweh, to do that which is evil in his sight? You have struck Uriah the Hittite with the sword, and have taken his wife to be your wife, and have slain him with the sword of the children of Ammon.

title: 2 Samuel 12:10
text: Now therefore the sword will never depart from your house, because you have despised me, and have taken the wife of Uriah the Hittite to be your wife.'

title: 2 Samuel 12:11
text: "This is what Yahweh says: 'Behold, I will raise up evil against you out of your own house; and I will take your wives before your eyes, and give them to your neighbor, and he will lie with your wives in the sight of this sun.

title: 2 Samuel 12:12
text: For you did it secretly, but I will do this thing before all Israel, and before the sun.'"

title: 2 Samuel 12:13
text: David said to Nathan, "I have sinned against Yahweh." Nathan said to David, "Yahweh also has put away your sin. You will not die.

title: 2 Samuel 12:14
text: However, because by this deed you have given great occasion to Yahweh's enemies to blaspheme, the child also who is born to you shall surely die."

title: 2 Samuel 12:15
text: Nathan departed to his house. Yahweh struck the child that Uriah's wife bore to David, and it was very sick.

title: 2 Samuel 12:16
text: David therefore begged God for the child; and David fasted, and went in, and lay all night on the earth.

title: 2 Samuel 12:17
text: The elders of his house arose, [and stood] beside him, to raise him up from the earth: but he would not, neither did he eat bread with them.

title: 2 Samuel 12:18
text: It happened on the seventh day, that the child died. The servants of David feared to tell him that the child was dead; for they said, "Behold, while the child was yet alive, we spoke to him, and he didn't listen to our voice. How will he then harm himself, if we tell him that the child is dead?"

title: 2 Samuel 12:19
text: But when David saw that his servants were whispering together, David perceived that the child was dead; and David said to his servants, "Is the child dead?" They said, "He is dead."

title: 2 Samuel 12:20
text: Then David arose from the earth, and washed, and anointed himself, and changed his clothing; and he came into the house of Yahweh, and worshiped: then he came to his own house; and when he required, they set bread before him, and he ate.

title: 2 Samuel 12:21
text: Then his servants said to him, "What is this that you have done? You fasted and wept for the child while he was alive; but when the child was dead, you rose up and ate bread."

title: 2 Samuel 12:22
text: He said, "While the child was yet alive, I fasted and wept; for I said, 'Who knows whether Yahweh will not be gracious to me, that the child may live?'

title: 2 Samuel 12:23
text: But now he is dead, why should I fast? Can I bring him back again? I shall go to him, but he will not return to me."

title: 2 Samuel 12:24
text: David comforted Bathsheba his wife, and went in to her, and lay with her. She bore a son, and he called his name Solomon. Yahweh loved him;

title: 2 Samuel 12:25
text: and he sent by the hand of Nathan the prophet; and he named him Jedidiah, for Yahweh's sake.

title: 2 Samuel 12:26
text: Now Joab fought against Rabbah of the children of Ammon, and took the royal city.

title: 2 Samuel 12:27
text: Joab sent messengers to David, and said, "I have fought against Rabbah. Yes, I have taken the city of waters.

title: 2 Samuel 12:28
text: Now therefore gather the rest of the people together, and encamp against the city, and take it; lest I take the city, and it be called after my name."

title: 2 Samuel 12:29
text: David gathered all the people together, and went to Rabbah, and fought against it, and took it.

title: 2 Samuel 12:30
text: He took the crown of their king from off his head; and its weight was a talent of gold, and [in it were] precious stones; and it was set on David's head. He brought forth the spoil of the city, exceeding much.

title: 2 Samuel 12:31
text: He brought forth the people who were therein, and put them under saws, and under iron picks, and under axes of iron, and made them pass through the brick kiln: and he did so to all the cities of the children of Ammon. David and all the people returned to Jerusalem.

title: 2 Samuel 13:1
text: It happened after this, that Absalom the son of David had a beautiful sister, whose name was Tamar; and Amnon the son of David loved her.

title: 2 Samuel 13:2
text: Amnon was so troubled that he fell sick because of his sister Tamar; for she was a virgin; and it seemed hard to Amnon to do anything to her.

title: 2 Samuel 13:3
text: But Amnon had a friend, whose name was Jonadab, the son of Shimeah, David's brother; and Jonadab was a very subtle man.

title: 2 Samuel 13:4
text: He said to him, "Why, son of the king, are you so sad from day to day? Won't you tell me?" Amnon said to him, "I love Tamar, my brother Absalom's sister."

title: 2 Samuel 13:5
text: Jonadab said to him, "Lay down on your bed, and pretend to be sick. When your father comes to see you, tell him, 'Please let my sister Tamar come and give me bread to eat, and dress the food in my sight, that I may see it, and eat it from her hand.'"

title: 2 Samuel 13:6
text: So Amnon lay down and faked being sick. When the king came to see him, Amnon said to the king, "Please let my sister Tamar come, and make me a couple of cakes in my sight, that I may eat from her hand."

title: 2 Samuel 13:7
text: Then David sent home to Tamar, saying, "Go now to your brother Amnon's house, and prepare food for him."

title: 2 Samuel 13:8
text: So Tamar went to her brother Amnon's house; and he was laid down. She took dough, and kneaded it, and made cakes in his sight, and baked the cakes.

title: 2 Samuel 13:9
text: She took the pan, and poured them out before him; but he refused to eat. Amnon said, "Have all men leave me." Every man went out from him.

title: 2 Samuel 13:10
text: Amnon said to Tamar, "Bring the food into the room, that I may eat from your hand." Tamar took the cakes which she had made, and brought them into the room to Amnon her brother.

title: 2 Samuel 13:11
text: When she had brought them near to him to eat, he took hold of her, and said to her, "Come, lie with me, my sister!"

title: 2 Samuel 13:12
text: She answered him, "No, my brother, do not force me! For no such thing ought to be done in Israel. Don't you do this folly.

title: 2 Samuel 13:13
text: I, where would I carry my shame? And as for you, you will be as one of the fools in Israel. Now therefore, please speak to the king; for he will not withhold me from you."

title: 2 Samuel 13:14
text: However he would not listen to her voice; but being stronger than she, he forced her, and lay with her.

title: 2 Samuel 13:15
text: Then Amnon hated her with exceeding great hatred; for the hatred with which he hated her was greater than the love with which he had loved her. Amnon said to her, "Arise, be gone!"

title: 2 Samuel 13:16
text: She said to him, "Not so, because this great wrong in sending me away is worse than the other that you did to me!" But he would not listen to her.

title: 2 Samuel 13:17
text: Then he called his servant who ministered to him, and said, "Put now this woman out from me, and bolt the door after her."

title: 2 Samuel 13:18
text: She had a garment of various colors on her; for with such robes were the king's daughters who were virgins dressed. Then his servant brought her out, and bolted the door after her.

title: 2 Samuel 13:19
text: Tamar put ashes on her head, and tore her garment of various colors that was on her; and she laid her hand on her head, and went her way, crying aloud as she went.

title: 2 Samuel 13:20
text: Absalom her brother said to her, "Has Amnon your brother been with you? But now hold your peace, my sister. He is your brother. Don't take this thing to heart." So Tamar remained desolate in her brother Absalom's house.

title: 2 Samuel 13:21
text: But when king David heard of all these things, he was very angry.

title: 2 Samuel 13:22
text: Absalom spoke to Amnon neither good nor bad; for Absalom hated Amnon, because he had forced his sister Tamar.

title: 2 Samuel 13:23
text: It happened after two full years, that Absalom had sheepshearers in Baal Hazor, which is beside Ephraim: and Absalom invited all the king's sons.

title: 2 Samuel 13:24
text: Absalom came to the king, and said, "See now, your servant has sheepshearers. Please let the king and his servants go with your servant."

title: 2 Samuel 13:25
text: The king said to Absalom, "No, my son, let us not all go, lest we be burdensome to you." He pressed him; however he would not go, but blessed him.

title: 2 Samuel 13:26
text: Then Absalom said, "If not, please let my brother Amnon go with us." The king said to him, "Why should he go with you?"

title: 2 Samuel 13:27
text: But Absalom pressed him, and he let Amnon and all the king's sons go with him.

title: 2 Samuel 13:28
text: Absalom commanded his servants, saying, "Mark now, when Amnon's heart is merry with wine; and when I tell you, 'Strike Amnon,' then kill him. Don't be afraid. Haven't I commanded you? Be courageous, and be valiant!"

title: 2 Samuel 13:29
text: The servants of Absalom did to Amnon as Absalom had commanded. Then all the king's sons arose, and every man got up on his mule, and fled.

title: 2 Samuel 13:30
text: It happened, while they were in the way, that the news came to David, saying, "Absalom has slain all the king's sons, and there is not one of them left!"

title: 2 Samuel 13:31
text: Then the king arose, and tore his garments, and lay on the earth; and all his servants stood by with their clothes torn.

title: 2 Samuel 13:32
text: Jonadab, the son of Shimeah, David's brother, answered, "Don't let my lord suppose that they have killed all the young men the king's sons; for Amnon only is dead; for by the appointment of Absalom this has been determined from the day that he forced his sister Tamar.

title: 2 Samuel 13:33
text: Now therefore don't let my lord the king take the thing to his heart, to think that all the king's sons are dead; for Amnon only is dead."

title: 2 Samuel 13:34
text: But Absalom fled. The young man who kept the watch lifted up his eyes, and looked, and behold, many people were coming by way of the hillside behind him.

title: 2 Samuel 13:35
text: Jonadab said to the king, "Behold, the king's sons are coming! It is as your servant said."

title: 2 Samuel 13:36
text: It happened, as soon as he had finished speaking, that behold, the king's sons came, and lifted up their voice, and wept. The king also and all his servants wept bitterly.

title: 2 Samuel 13:37
text: But Absalom fled, and went to Talmai the son of Ammihur, king of Geshur. David mourned for his son every day.

title: 2 Samuel 13:38
text: So Absalom fled, and went to Geshur, and was there three years.

title: 2 Samuel 13:39
text: [the soul of] king David longed to go forth to Absalom: for he was comforted concerning Amnon, since he was dead.

title: 2 Samuel 14:1
text: Now Joab the son of Zeruiah perceived that the king's heart was toward Absalom.

title: 2 Samuel 14:2
text: Joab sent to Tekoa, and fetched there a wise woman, and said to her, "Please act like a mourner, and put on mourning clothing, please, and don't anoint yourself with oil, but be as a woman who has mourned a long time for the dead.

title: 2 Samuel 14:3
text: Go in to the king, and speak like this to him." So Joab put the words in her mouth.

title: 2 Samuel 14:4
text: When the woman of Tekoa spoke to the king, she fell on her face to the ground, and did obeisance, and said, "Help, O king!"

title: 2 Samuel 14:5
text: The king said to her, "What ails you?" She answered, "Truly I am a widow, and my husband is dead.

title: 2 Samuel 14:6
text: Your handmaid had two sons, and they both fought together in the field, and there was no one to part them, but the one struck the other, and killed him.

title: 2 Samuel 14:7
text: Behold, the whole family has risen against your handmaid, and they say, 'Deliver him who struck his brother, that we may kill him for the life of his brother whom he killed, and so destroy the heir also.' Thus they would quench my coal which is left, and would leave to my husband neither name nor remainder on the surface of the earth."

title: 2 Samuel 14:8
text: The king said to the woman, "Go to your house, and I will give a command concerning you."

title: 2 Samuel 14:9
text: The woman of Tekoa said to the king, "My lord, O king, the iniquity be on me, and on my father's house; and the king and his throne be guiltless."

title: 2 Samuel 14:10
text: The king said, "Whoever says anything to you, bring him to me, and he shall not touch you any more."

title: 2 Samuel 14:11
text: Then she said, "Please let the king remember Yahweh your God, that the avenger of blood destroy not any more, lest they destroy my son." He said, "As Yahweh lives, not one hair of your son shall fall to the earth."

title: 2 Samuel 14:12
text: Then the woman said, "Please let your handmaid speak a word to my lord the king." He said, "Say on."

title: 2 Samuel 14:13
text: The woman said, "Why then have you devised such a thing against the people of God? For in speaking this word the king is as one who is guilty, in that the king does not bring home again his banished one.

title: 2 Samuel 14:14
text: For we must die, and are as water split on the ground, which can't be gathered up again; neither does God take away life, but devises means, that he who is banished not be an outcast from him.

title: 2 Samuel 14:15
text: Now therefore seeing that I have come to speak this word to my lord the king, it is because the people have made me afraid: and your handmaid said, 'I will now speak to the king; it may be that the king will perform the request of his servant.'

title: 2 Samuel 14:16
text: For the king will hear, to deliver his servant out of the hand of the man who would destroy me and my son together out of the inheritance of God.

title: 2 Samuel 14:17
text: Then your handmaid said, 'Please let the word of my lord the king bring rest; for as an angel of God, so is my lord the king to discern good and bad. May Yahweh, your God, be with you.'"

title: 2 Samuel 14:18
text: Then the king answered the woman, "Please don't hide anything from me that I ask you." The woman said, "Let my lord the king now speak."

title: 2 Samuel 14:19
text: The king said, "Is the hand of Joab with you in all this?" The woman answered, "As your soul lives, my lord the king, no one can turn to the right hand or to the left from anything that my lord the king has spoken; for your servant Joab, he urged me, and he put all these words in the mouth of your handmaid;

title: 2 Samuel 14:20
text: to change the face of the matter has your servant Joab done this thing. My lord is wise, according to the wisdom of an angel of God, to know all things that are in the earth."

title: 2 Samuel 14:21
text: The king said to Joab, "Behold now, I have done this thing. Go therefore, bring the young man Absalom back."

title: 2 Samuel 14:22
text: Joab fell to the ground on his face, and did obeisance, and blessed the king. Joab said, "Today your servant knows that I have found favor in your sight, my lord, king, in that the king has performed the request of his servant."

title: 2 Samuel 14:23
text: So Joab arose and went to Geshur, and brought Absalom to Jerusalem.

title: 2 Samuel 14:24
text: The king said, "Let him return to his own house, but let him not see my face." So Absalom returned to his own house, and didn't see the king's face.

title: 2 Samuel 14:25
text: Now in all Israel there was none to be so much praised as Absalom for his beauty: from the sole of his foot even to the crown of his head there was no blemish in him.

title: 2 Samuel 14:26
text: When he cut the hair of his head (now it was at every year's end that he cut it; because it was heavy on him, therefore he cut it); he weighed the hair of his head at two hundred shekels, after the king's weight.

title: 2 Samuel 14:27
text: To Absalom there were born three sons, and one daughter, whose name was Tamar: she was a woman of a beautiful face.

title: 2 Samuel 14:28
text: Absalom lived two full years in Jerusalem; and he didn't see the king's face.

title: 2 Samuel 14:29
text: Then Absalom sent for Joab, to send him to the king; but he would not come to him: and he sent again a second time, but he would not come.

title: 2 Samuel 14:30
text: Therefore he said to his servants, "Behold, Joab's field is near mine, and he has barley there. Go and set it on fire." Absalom's servants set the field on fire.

title: 2 Samuel 14:31
text: Then Joab arose, and came to Absalom to his house, and said to him, "Why have your servants set my field on fire?"

title: 2 Samuel 14:32
text: Absalom answered Joab, "Behold, I sent to you, saying, 'Come here, that I may send you to the king, to say, "Why have I come from Geshur? It would be better for me to be there still. Now therefore let me see the king's face; and if there is iniquity in me, let him kill me."'"

title: 2 Samuel 14:33
text: So Joab came to the king, and told him; and when he had called for Absalom, he came to the king, and bowed himself on his face to the ground before the king: and the king kissed Absalom.

title: 2 Samuel 15:1
text: It happened after this, that Absalom prepared him a chariot and horses, and fifty men to run before him.

title: 2 Samuel 15:2
text: Absalom rose up early, and stood beside the way of the gate. It was so, that when any man had a suit which should come to the king for judgment, then Absalom called to him, and said, "What city are you from?" He said, "Your servant is of one of the tribes of Israel."

title: 2 Samuel 15:3
text: Absalom said to him, "Behold, your matters are good and right; but there is no man deputized by the king to hear you."

title: 2 Samuel 15:4
text: Absalom said moreover, "Oh that I were made judge in the land, that every man who has any suit or cause might come to me, and I would do him justice!"

title: 2 Samuel 15:5
text: It was so, that when any man came near to do him obeisance, he put forth his hand, and took hold of him, and kissed him.

title: 2 Samuel 15:6
text: Absalom did this sort of thing to all Israel who came to the king for judgment. So Absalom stole the hearts of the men of Israel.

title: 2 Samuel 15:7
text: It happened at the end of forty years, that Absalom said to the king, "Please let me go and pay my vow, which I have vowed to Yahweh, in Hebron.

title: 2 Samuel 15:8
text: For your servant vowed a vow while I stayed at Geshur in Syria, saying, 'If Yahweh shall indeed bring me again to Jerusalem, then I will serve Yahweh.'"

title: 2 Samuel 15:9
text: The king said to him, "Go in peace." So he arose, and went to Hebron.

title: 2 Samuel 15:10
text: But Absalom sent spies throughout all the tribes of Israel, saying, "As soon as you hear the sound of the trumpet, then you shall say, 'Absalom is king in Hebron!'"

title: 2 Samuel 15:11
text: Two hundred men went with Absalom out of Jerusalem, who were invited, and went in their simplicity; and they didn't know anything.

title: 2 Samuel 15:12
text: Absalom sent for Ahithophel the Gilonite, David's counselor, from his city, even from Giloh, while he was offering the sacrifices. The conspiracy was strong; for the people increased continually with Absalom.

title: 2 Samuel 15:13
text: A messenger came to David, saying, "The hearts of the men of Israel are after Absalom."

title: 2 Samuel 15:14
text: David said to all his servants who were with him at Jerusalem, "Arise, and let us flee; for else none of us shall escape from Absalom. Make speed to depart, lest he overtake us quickly, and bring down evil on us, and strike the city with the edge of the sword."

title: 2 Samuel 15:15
text: The king's servants said to the king, "Behold, your servants are ready to do whatever my lord the king chooses."

title: 2 Samuel 15:16
text: The king went forth, and all his household after him. The king left ten women, who were concubines, to keep the house.

title: 2 Samuel 15:17
text: The king went forth, and all the people after him; and they stayed in Beth Merhak.

title: 2 Samuel 15:18
text: All his servants passed on beside him; and all the Cherethites, and all the Pelethites, and all the Gittites, six hundred men who came after him from Gath, passed on before the king.

title: 2 Samuel 15:19
text: Then the king said to Ittai the Gittite, "Why do you also go with us? Return, and stay with the king; for you are a foreigner, and also an exile. Return to your own place.

title: 2 Samuel 15:20
text: Whereas you came but yesterday, should I this day make you go up and down with us, since I go where I may? Return, and take back your brothers. Mercy and truth be with you."

title: 2 Samuel 15:21
text: Ittai answered the king, and said, "As Yahweh lives, and as my lord the king lives, surely in what place my lord the king shall is, whether for death or for life, even there also will your servant be."

title: 2 Samuel 15:22
text: David said to Ittai, "Go and pass over." Ittai the Gittite passed over, and all his men, and all the little ones who were with him.

title: 2 Samuel 15:23
text: All the country wept with a loud voice, and all the people passed over: the king also himself passed over the brook Kidron, and all the people passed over, toward the way of the wilderness.

title: 2 Samuel 15:24
text: Behold, Zadok also came, and all the Levites with him, bearing the ark of the covenant of God; and they set down the ark of God; and Abiathar went up, until all the people finished passing out of the city.

title: 2 Samuel 15:25
text: The king said to Zadok, "Carry back the ark of God into the city. If I find favor in the eyes of Yahweh, he will bring me again, and show me both it, and his habitation;

title: 2 Samuel 15:26
text: but if he say thus, 'I have no delight in you;' behold, here am I. Let him do to me as seems good to him."

title: 2 Samuel 15:27
text: The king said also to Zadok the priest, "Aren't you a seer? Return into the city in peace, and your two sons with you, Ahimaaz your son, and Jonathan the son of Abiathar.

title: 2 Samuel 15:28
text: Behold, I will stay at the fords of the wilderness, until word comes from you to inform me."

title: 2 Samuel 15:29
text: Zadok therefore and Abiathar carried the ark of God again to Jerusalem; and they stayed there.

title: 2 Samuel 15:30
text: David went up by the ascent of the [Mount of] Olives, and wept as he went up; and he had his head covered, and went barefoot: and all the people who were with him covered every man his head, and they went up, weeping as they went up.

title: 2 Samuel 15:31
text: Someone told David, saying, "Ahithophel is among the conspirators with Absalom." David said, "Yahweh, please turn the counsel of Ahithophel into foolishness."

title: 2 Samuel 15:32
text: It happened that when David had come to the top [of the ascent], where God was worshiped, behold, Hushai the Archite came to meet him with his coat torn, and earth on his head.

title: 2 Samuel 15:33
text: David said to him, "If you pass on with me, then you will be a burden to me;

title: 2 Samuel 15:34
text: but if you return to the city, and tell Absalom, 'I will be your servant, O king. As I have been your father's servant in time past, so will I now be your servant; then will you defeat for me the counsel of Ahithophel.'

title: 2 Samuel 15:35
text: Don't you have Zadok and Abiathar the priests there with you? Therefore it shall be, that whatever thing you shall hear out of the king's house, you shall tell it to Zadok and Abiathar the priests.

title: 2 Samuel 15:36
text: Behold, they have there with them their two sons, Ahimaaz, Zadok's son, and Jonathan, Abiathar's son; and by them you shall send to me everything that you shall hear."

title: 2 Samuel 15:37
text: So Hushai, David's friend, came into the city; and Absalom came into Jerusalem.

title: 2 Samuel 16:1
text: When David was a little past the top [of the ascent], behold, Ziba the servant of Mephibosheth met him, with a couple of donkeys saddled, and on them two hundred loaves of bread, and one hundred clusters of raisins, and one hundred summer fruits, and a bottle of wine.

title: 2 Samuel 16:2
text: The king said to Ziba, What do you mean by these? Ziba said, The donkeys are for the king's household to ride on; and the bread and summer fruit for the young men to eat; and the wine, that such as are faint in the wilderness may drink.

title: 2 Samuel 16:3
text: The king said, "Where is your master's son?" Ziba said to the king, "Behold, he is staying in Jerusalem; for he said, 'Today the house of Israel will restore me the kingdom of my father.'"

title: 2 Samuel 16:4
text: Then the king said to Ziba, "Behold, all that pertains to Mephibosheth is yours." Ziba said, "I do obeisance. Let me find favor in your sight, my lord, O king."

title: 2 Samuel 16:5
text: When king David came to Bahurim, behold, a man of the family of the house of Saul came out, whose name was Shimei, the son of Gera. He came out, and cursed still as he came.

title: 2 Samuel 16:6
text: He cast stones at David, and at all the servants of king David, and all the people and all the mighty men were on his right hand and on his left.

title: 2 Samuel 16:7
text: Shimei said when he cursed, "Be gone, be gone, you man of blood, and base fellow!

title: 2 Samuel 16:8
text: Yahweh has returned on you all the blood of the house of Saul, in whose place you have reigned! Yahweh has delivered the kingdom into the hand of Absalom your son! Behold, you are caught by your own mischief, because you are a man of blood!"

title: 2 Samuel 16:9
text: Then Abishai the son of Zeruiah said to the king, "Why should this dead dog curse my lord the king? Please let me go over and take off his head."

title: 2 Samuel 16:10
text: The king said, "What have I to do with you, you sons of Zeruiah? Because he curses, and because Yahweh has said to him, 'Curse David;' who then shall say, 'Why have you done so?'"

title: 2 Samuel 16:11
text: David said to Abishai, and to all his servants, "Behold, my son, who came forth from my bowels, seeks my life. How much more this Benjamite, now? Leave him alone, and let him curse; for Yahweh has invited him.

title: 2 Samuel 16:12
text: It may be that Yahweh will look on the wrong done to me, and that Yahweh will repay me good for the cursing of me today."

title: 2 Samuel 16:13
text: So David and his men went by the way; and Shimei went along on the hillside opposite him, and cursed as he went, threw stones at him, and threw dust.

title: 2 Samuel 16:14
text: The king, and all the people who were with him, came weary; and he refreshed himself there.

title: 2 Samuel 16:15
text: Absalom, and all the people, the men of Israel, came to Jerusalem, and Ahithophel with him.

title: 2 Samuel 16:16
text: It happened, when Hushai the Archite, David's friend, had come to Absalom, that Hushai said to Absalom, "Long live the king! Long live the king!"

title: 2 Samuel 16:17
text: Absalom said to Hushai, "Is this your kindness to your friend? Why didn't you go with your friend?"

title: 2 Samuel 16:18
text: Hushai said to Absalom, "No; but whoever Yahweh, and this people, and all the men of Israel have chosen, his will I be, and with him I will stay.

title: 2 Samuel 16:19
text: Again, whom should I serve? Shouldn't I serve in the presence of his son? As I have served in your father's presence, so will I be in your presence."

title: 2 Samuel 16:20
text: Then Absalom said to Ahithophel, "Give your counsel what we shall do."

title: 2 Samuel 16:21
text: Ahithophel said to Absalom, "Go in to your father's concubines, that he has left to keep the house. Then all Israel will hear that you are abhorred by your father. Then the hands of all who are with you will be strong."

title: 2 Samuel 16:22
text: So they spread Absalom a tent on the top of the house; and Absalom went in to his father's concubines in the sight of all Israel.

title: 2 Samuel 16:23
text: The counsel of Ahithophel, which he gave in those days, was as if a man inquired at the oracle of God: so was all the counsel of Ahithophel both with David and with Absalom.

title: 2 Samuel 17:1
text: Moreover Ahithophel said to Absalom, "Let me now choose twelve thousand men, and I will arise and pursue after David tonight.

title: 2 Samuel 17:2
text: I will come on him while he is weary and exhausted, and will make him afraid. All the people who are with him shall flee. I will strike the king only;

title: 2 Samuel 17:3
text: and I will bring back all the people to you. The man whom you seek is as if all returned. All the people shall be in peace."

title: 2 Samuel 17:4
text: The saying pleased Absalom well, and all the elders of Israel.

title: 2 Samuel 17:5
text: Then Absalom said, "Now call Hushai the Archite also, and let us hear likewise what he says."

title: 2 Samuel 17:6
text: When Hushai was come to Absalom, Absalom spoke to him, saying, "Ahithophel has spoken like this. Shall we do what he says? If not, speak up."

title: 2 Samuel 17:7
text: Hushai said to Absalom, "The counsel that Ahithophel has given this time is not good."

title: 2 Samuel 17:8
text: Hushai said moreover, "You know your father and his men, that they are mighty men, and they are fierce in their minds, like a bear robbed of her cubs in the field. Your father is a man of war, and will not lodge with the people.

title: 2 Samuel 17:9
text: Behold, he is now hidden in some pit, or in some other place. It will happen, when some of them have fallen at the first, that whoever hears it will say, 'There is a slaughter among the people who follow Absalom!'

title: 2 Samuel 17:10
text: Even he who is valiant, whose heart is as the heart of a lion, will utterly melt; for all Israel knows that your father is a mighty man, and those who are with him are valiant men.

title: 2 Samuel 17:11
text: But I counsel that all Israel be gathered together to you, from Dan even to Beersheba, as the sand that is by the sea for multitude; and that you go to battle in your own person.

title: 2 Samuel 17:12
text: So shall we come on him in some place where he shall be found, and we will light on him as the dew falls on the ground; and of him and of all the men who are with him we will not leave so much as one.

title: 2 Samuel 17:13
text: Moreover, if he be gone into a city, then shall all Israel bring ropes to that city, and we will draw it into the river, until there isn't one small stone found there."

title: 2 Samuel 17:14
text: Absalom and all the men of Israel said, "The counsel of Hushai the Archite is better than the counsel of Ahithophel." For Yahweh had ordained to defeat the good counsel of Ahithophel, to the intent that Yahweh might bring evil on Absalom.

title: 2 Samuel 17:15
text: Then Hushai said to Zadok and to Abiathar the priests, "Ahithophel counseled Absalom and the elders of Israel that way; and I have counseled this way.

title: 2 Samuel 17:16
text: Now therefore send quickly, and tell David, saying, 'Don't lodge this night at the fords of the wilderness, but by all means pass over; lest the king be swallowed up, and all the people who are with him.'"

title: 2 Samuel 17:17
text: Now Jonathan and Ahimaaz were staying by En Rogel; and a female servant used to go and tell them; and they went and told king David. For they might not be seen to come into the city.

title: 2 Samuel 17:18
text: But a boy saw them, and told Absalom. Then they both went away quickly, and came to the house of a man in Bahurim, who had a well in his court; and they went down there.

title: 2 Samuel 17:19
text: The woman took and spread the covering over the well's mouth, and spread out bruised grain on it; and nothing was known.

title: 2 Samuel 17:20
text: Absalom's servants came to the woman to the house; and they said, "Where are Ahimaaz and Jonathan?" The woman said to them, "They have gone over the brook of water." When they had sought and could not find them, they returned to Jerusalem.

title: 2 Samuel 17:21
text: It happened, after they had departed, that they came up out of the well, and went and told king David; and they said to David, "Arise and pass quickly over the water; for thus has Ahithophel counseled against you."

title: 2 Samuel 17:22
text: Then David arose, and all the people who were with him, and they passed over the Jordan. By the morning light there lacked not one of them who had not gone over the Jordan.

title: 2 Samuel 17:23
text: When Ahithophel saw that his counsel was not followed, he saddled his donkey, and arose, and went home, to his city, and set his house in order, and hanged himself; and he died, and was buried in the tomb of his father.

title: 2 Samuel 17:24
text: Then David came to Mahanaim. Absalom passed over the Jordan, he and all the men of Israel with him.

title: 2 Samuel 17:25
text: Absalom set Amasa over the army instead of Joab. Now Amasa was the son of a man, whose name was Ithra the Israelite, who went in to Abigail the daughter of Nahash, sister to Zeruiah, Joab's mother.

title: 2 Samuel 17:26
text: Israel and Absalom encamped in the land of Gilead.

title: 2 Samuel 17:27
text: It happened, when David was come to Mahanaim, that Shobi the son of Nahash of Rabbah of the children of Ammon, and Machir the son of Ammiel of Lodebar, and Barzillai the Gileadite of Rogelim,

title: 2 Samuel 17:28
text: brought beds, and basins, and earthen vessels, and wheat, and barley, and meal, and parched [grain], and beans, and lentils, and parched [pulse],

title: 2 Samuel 17:29
text: and honey, and butter, and sheep, and cheese of the herd, for David, and for the people who were with him, to eat: for they said, "The people are hungry, and weary, and thirsty, in the wilderness."

title: 2 Samuel 18:1
text: David numbered the people who were with him, and set captains of thousands and captains of hundreds over them.

title: 2 Samuel 18:2
text: David sent forth the people, a third part under the hand of Joab, and a third part under the hand of Abishai the son of Zeruiah, Joab's brother, and a third part under the hand of Ittai the Gittite. The king said to the people, "I will surely go forth with you myself also."

title: 2 Samuel 18:3
text: But the people said, "You shall not go forth; for if we flee away, they will not care for us; neither if half of us die, will they care for us. But you are worth ten thousand of us. Therefore now it is better that you are ready to help us out of the city."

title: 2 Samuel 18:4
text: The king said to them, "I will do what seems best to you." The king stood beside the gate, and all the people went out by hundreds and by thousands.

title: 2 Samuel 18:5
text: The king commanded Joab and Abishai and Ittai, saying, "Deal gently for my sake with the young man, even with Absalom." All the people heard when the king commanded all the captains concerning Absalom.

title: 2 Samuel 18:6
text: So the people went out into the field against Israel: and the battle was in the forest of Ephraim.

title: 2 Samuel 18:7
text: The people of Israel were struck there before the servants of David, and there was a great slaughter there that day of twenty thousand men.

title: 2 Samuel 18:8
text: For the battle was there spread over the surface of all the country; and the forest devoured more people that day than the sword devoured.

title: 2 Samuel 18:9
text: Absalom happened to meet the servants of David. Absalom was riding on his mule, and the mule went under the thick boughs of a great oak, and his head caught hold of the oak, and he was taken up between the sky and earth; and the mule that was under him went on.

title: 2 Samuel 18:10
text: A certain man saw it, and told Joab, and said, "Behold, I saw Absalom hanging in an oak."

title: 2 Samuel 18:11
text: Joab said to the man who told him, "Behold, you saw it, and why didn't you strike him there to the ground? I would have given you ten pieces of silver, and a sash."

title: 2 Samuel 18:12
text: The man said to Joab, "Though I should receive a thousand pieces of silver in my hand, I still wouldn't put forth my hand against the king's son; for in our hearing the king commanded you and Abishai and Ittai, saying, 'Beware that none touch the young man Absalom.'

title: 2 Samuel 18:13
text: Otherwise if I had dealt falsely against his life (and there is no matter hidden from the king), then you yourself would have set yourself against me."

title: 2 Samuel 18:14
text: Then Joab said, "I'm not going to wait like this with you." He took three darts in his hand, and thrust them through the heart of Absalom, while he was yet alive in the midst of the oak.

title: 2 Samuel 18:15
text: Ten young men who bore Joab's armor surrounded and struck Absalom, and killed him.

title: 2 Samuel 18:16
text: Joab blew the trumpet, and the people returned from pursuing after Israel; for Joab held back the people.

title: 2 Samuel 18:17
text: They took Absalom, and cast him into the great pit in the forest, and raised over him a very great heap of stones. Then all Israel fled everyone to his tent.

title: 2 Samuel 18:18
text: Now Absalom in his lifetime had taken and reared up for himself the pillar, which is in the king's dale; for he said, "I have no son to keep my name in memory." He called the pillar after his own name; and it is called Absalom's monument, to this day.

title: 2 Samuel 18:19
text: Then Ahimaaz the son of Zadok said, "Let me now run, and bear the king news, how that Yahweh has avenged him of his enemies."

title: 2 Samuel 18:20
text: Joab said to him, "You shall not be the bearer of news this day, but you shall bear news another day. But today you shall bear no news, because the king's son is dead."

title: 2 Samuel 18:21
text: Then Joab said to the Cushite, "Go, tell the king what you have seen!" The Cushite bowed himself to Joab, and ran.

title: 2 Samuel 18:22
text: Then Ahimaaz the son of Zadok said yet again to Joab, "But come what may, please let me also run after the Cushite." Joab said, "Why do you want to run, my son, since that you will have no reward for the news?"

title: 2 Samuel 18:23
text: "But come what may," he said, "I will run." He said to him, "Run!" Then Ahimaaz ran by the way of the Plain, and outran the Cushite.

title: 2 Samuel 18:24
text: Now David was sitting between the two gates: and the watchman went up to the roof of the gate to the wall, and lifted up his eyes, and looked, and, behold, a man running alone.

title: 2 Samuel 18:25
text: The watchman cried, and told the king. The king said, "If he is alone, there is news in his mouth." He came closer and closer.

title: 2 Samuel 18:26
text: The watchman saw another man running; and the watchman called to the porter, and said, "Behold, a man running alone!" The king said, "He also brings news."

title: 2 Samuel 18:27
text: The watchman said, "I think the running of the first one is like the running of Ahimaaz the son of Zadok." The king said, "He is a good man, and comes with good news."

title: 2 Samuel 18:28
text: Ahimaaz called, and said to the king, "All is well." He bowed himself before the king with his face to the earth, and said, "Blessed is Yahweh your God, who has delivered up the men who lifted up their hand against my lord the king!"

title: 2 Samuel 18:29
text: The king said, "Is it well with the young man Absalom?" Ahimaaz answered, "When Joab sent the king's servant, even me your servant, I saw a great tumult, but I don't know what it was."

title: 2 Samuel 18:30
text: The king said, "Turn aside, and stand here." He turned aside, and stood still.

title: 2 Samuel 18:31
text: Behold, the Cushite came. The Cushite said, "News for my lord the king; for Yahweh has avenged you this day of all those who rose up against you."

title: 2 Samuel 18:32
text: The king said to the Cushite, "Is it well with the young man Absalom?" The Cushite answered, "May the enemies of my lord the king, and all who rise up against you to do you harm, be as that young man is."

title: 2 Samuel 18:33
text: The king was much moved, and went up to the room over the gate, and wept. As he went, he said, "My son Absalom! My son, my son Absalom! I wish I had died for you, Absalom, my son, my son!"

title: 2 Samuel 19:1
text: It was told Joab, "Behold, the king weeps and mourns for Absalom."

title: 2 Samuel 19:2
text: The victory that day was turned into mourning to all the people; for the people heard it said that day, "The king grieves for his son."

title: 2 Samuel 19:3
text: The people snuck into the city that day, as people who are ashamed steal away when they flee in battle.

title: 2 Samuel 19:4
text: The king covered his face, and the king cried with a loud voice, "My son Absalom, Absalom, my son, my son!"

title: 2 Samuel 19:5
text: Joab came into the house to the king, and said, "You have shamed this day the faces of all your servants, who this day have saved your life, and the lives of your sons and of your daughters, and the lives of your wives, and the lives of your concubines;

title: 2 Samuel 19:6
text: in that you love those who hate you, and hate those who love you. For you have declared this day, that princes and servants are nothing to you. For today I perceive that if Absalom had lived, and all we had died this day, then it would have pleased you well.

title: 2 Samuel 19:7
text: Now therefore arise, go out, and speak to comfort your servants; for I swear by Yahweh, if you don't go out, not a man will stay with you this night. That would be worse to you than all the evil that has happened to you from your youth until now."

title: 2 Samuel 19:8
text: Then the king arose, and sat in the gate. They told to all the people, saying, "Behold, the king is sitting in the gate." All the people came before the king. Now Israel had fled every man to his tent.

title: 2 Samuel 19:9
text: All the people were at strife throughout all the tribes of Israel, saying, "The king delivered us out of the hand of our enemies, and he saved us out of the hand of the Philistines; and now he has fled out of the land from Absalom.

title: 2 Samuel 19:10
text: Absalom, whom we anointed over us, is dead in battle. Now therefore why don't you speak a word of bringing the king back?"

title: 2 Samuel 19:11
text: King David sent to Zadok and to Abiathar the priests, saying, "Speak to the elders of Judah, saying, 'Why are you the last to bring the king back to his house? Since the speech of all Israel has come to the king, to return him to his house.

title: 2 Samuel 19:12
text: You are my brothers, you are my bone and my flesh. Why then are you the last to bring back the king?'

title: 2 Samuel 19:13
text: Say to Amasa, 'Aren't you my bone and my flesh? God do so to me, and more also, if you aren't captain of the army before me continually in the room of Joab.'"

title: 2 Samuel 19:14
text: He bowed the heart of all the men of Judah, even as [the heart of] one man; so that they sent to the king, saying, "Return, you and all your servants."

title: 2 Samuel 19:15
text: So the king returned, and came to the Jordan. Judah came to Gilgal, to go to meet the king, to bring the king over the Jordan.

title: 2 Samuel 19:16
text: Shimei the son of Gera, the Benjamite, who was of Bahurim, hurried and came down with the men of Judah to meet king David.

title: 2 Samuel 19:17
text: There were a thousand men of Benjamin with him, and Ziba the servant of the house of Saul, and his fifteen sons and his twenty servants with him; and they went through the Jordan in the presence of the king.

title: 2 Samuel 19:18
text: A ferry boat went to bring over the king's household, and to do what he thought good. Shimei the son of Gera fell down before the king, when he was come over the Jordan.

title: 2 Samuel 19:19
text: He said to the king, "Don't let my lord impute iniquity to me, neither do you remember that which your servant did perversely the day that my lord the king went out of Jerusalem, that the king should take it to his heart.

title: 2 Samuel 19:20
text: For your servant knows that I have sinned. Therefore, behold, I have come this day the first of all the house of Joseph to go down to meet my lord the king."

title: 2 Samuel 19:21
text: But Abishai the son of Zeruiah answered, "Shall Shimei not be put to death for this, because he cursed Yahweh's anointed?"

title: 2 Samuel 19:22
text: David said, "What have I to do with you, you sons of Zeruiah, that you should this day be adversaries to me? Shall there any man be put to death this day in Israel? For don't I know that I am this day king over Israel?"

title: 2 Samuel 19:23
text: The king said to Shimei, "You shall not die." The king swore to him.

title: 2 Samuel 19:24
text: Mephibosheth the son of Saul came down to meet the king; and he had neither groomed his feet, nor trimmed his beard, nor washed his clothes, from the day the king departed until the day he came home in peace.

title: 2 Samuel 19:25
text: It happened, when he had come to Jerusalem to meet the king, that the king said to him, "Why didn't you go with me, Mephibosheth?"

title: 2 Samuel 19:26
text: He answered, "My lord, O king, my servant deceived me. For your servant said, I will saddle me a donkey, that I may ride thereon, and go with the king; because your servant is lame.

title: 2 Samuel 19:27
text: He has slandered your servant to my lord the king; but my lord the king is as an angel of God. Do therefore what is good in your eyes.

title: 2 Samuel 19:28
text: For all my father's house were but dead men before my lord the king; yet you set your servant among those who ate at your own table. What right therefore have I yet that I should cry any more to the king?"

title: 2 Samuel 19:29
text: The king said to him, "Why do you speak any more of your matters? I say, you and Ziba divide the land."

title: 2 Samuel 19:30
text: Mephibosheth said to the king, "Yes, let him take all, because my lord the king has come in peace to his own house."

title: 2 Samuel 19:31
text: Barzillai the Gileadite came down from Rogelim; and he went over the Jordan with the king, to conduct him over the Jordan.

title: 2 Samuel 19:32
text: Now Barzillai was a very aged man, even eighty years old: and he had provided the king with sustenance while he lay at Mahanaim; for he was a very great man.

title: 2 Samuel 19:33
text: The king said to Barzillai, "Come over with me, and I will sustain you with me in Jerusalem."

title: 2 Samuel 19:34
text: Barzillai said to the king, "How many are the days of the years of my life, that I should go up with the king to Jerusalem?

title: 2 Samuel 19:35
text: I am this day eighty years old. Can I discern between good and bad? Can your servant taste what I eat or what I drink? Can I hear any more the voice of singing men and singing women? Why then should your servant be yet a burden to my lord the king?

title: 2 Samuel 19:36
text: Your servant would but just go over the Jordan with the king. Why should the king repay me with such a reward?

title: 2 Samuel 19:37
text: Please let your servant turn back again, that I may die in my own city, by the grave of my father and my mother. But behold, your servant Chimham; let him go over with my lord the king; and do to him what shall seem good to you."

title: 2 Samuel 19:38
text: The king answered, "Chimham shall go over with me, and I will do to him that which shall seem good to you. Whatever you require of me, that I will do for you."

title: 2 Samuel 19:39
text: All the people went over the Jordan, and the king went over. Then the king kissed Barzillai, and blessed him; and he returned to his own place.

title: 2 Samuel 19:40
text: So the king went over to Gilgal, and Chimham went over with him. All the people of Judah brought the king over, and also half the people of Israel.

title: 2 Samuel 19:41
text: Behold, all the men of Israel came to the king, and said to the king, "Why have our brothers the men of Judah stolen you away, and brought the king, and his household, over the Jordan, and all David's men with him?"

title: 2 Samuel 19:42
text: All the men of Judah answered the men of Israel, "Because the king is a close relative to us. Why then are you angry about this matter? Have we eaten at all at the king's cost? Or has he given us any gift?"

title: 2 Samuel 19:43
text: The men of Israel answered the men of Judah, and said, "We have ten parts in the king, and we have also more claim to David than you. Why then did you despise us, that our advice should not be first had in bringing back our king?" The words of the men of Judah were fiercer than the words of the men of Israel.

title: 2 Samuel 20:1
text: There happened to be there a base fellow, whose name was Sheba, the son of Bichri, a Benjamite: and he blew the trumpet, and said, "We have no portion in David, neither have we inheritance in the son of Jesse. Every man to his tents, Israel!"

title: 2 Samuel 20:2
text: So all the men of Israel went up from following David, and followed Sheba the son of Bichri; but the men of Judah joined with their king, from the Jordan even to Jerusalem.

title: 2 Samuel 20:3
text: David came to his house at Jerusalem; and the king took the ten women his concubines, whom he had left to keep the house, and put them in custody, and provided them with sustenance, but didn't go in to them. So they were shut up to the day of their death, living in widowhood.

title: 2 Samuel 20:4
text: Then the king said to Amasa, "Call me the men of Judah together within three days, and be here present."

title: 2 Samuel 20:5
text: So Amasa went to call [the men of] Judah together; but he stayed longer than the set time which he had appointed him.

title: 2 Samuel 20:6
text: David said to Abishai, "Now Sheba the son of Bichri will do us more harm than did Absalom. Take your lord's servants, and pursue after him, lest he get himself fortified cities, and escape out of our sight."

title: 2 Samuel 20:7
text: There went out after him Joab's men, and the Cherethites and the Pelethites, and all the mighty men; and they went out of Jerusalem, to pursue after Sheba the son of Bichri.

title: 2 Samuel 20:8
text: When they were at the great stone which is in Gibeon, Amasa came to meet them. Joab was clothed in his apparel of war that he had put on, and on it was a sash with a sword fastened on his waist in its sheath; and as he went forth it fell out.

title: 2 Samuel 20:9
text: Joab said to Amasa, "Is it well with you, my brother?" Joab took Amasa by the beard with his right hand to kiss him.

title: 2 Samuel 20:10
text: But Amasa took no heed to the sword that was in Joab's hand. So he struck him with it in the body, and shed out his bowels to the ground, and didn't strike him again; and he died. Joab and Abishai his brother pursued after Sheba the son of Bichri.

title: 2 Samuel 20:11
text: There stood by him one of Joab's young men, and said, "He who favors Joab, and he who is for David, let him follow Joab!"

title: 2 Samuel 20:12
text: Amasa lay wallowing in his blood in the midst of the highway. When the man saw that all the people stood still, he carried Amasa out of the highway into the field, and cast a garment over him, when he saw that everyone who came by him stood still.

title: 2 Samuel 20:13
text: When he was removed out of the highway, all the people went on after Joab, to pursue after Sheba the son of Bichri.

title: 2 Samuel 20:14
text: He went through all the tribes of Israel to Abel, and to Beth Maacah, and all the Berites: and they were gathered together, and went also after him.

title: 2 Samuel 20:15
text: They came and besieged him in Abel of Beth Maacah, and they cast up a mound against the city, and it stood against the rampart; and all the people who were with Joab battered the wall, to throw it down.

title: 2 Samuel 20:16
text: Then a wise woman cried out of the city, "Hear, hear! Please say to Joab, 'Come near here, that I may speak with you.'"

title: 2 Samuel 20:17
text: He came near to her; and the woman said, "Are you Joab?" He answered, "I am." Then she said to him, "Hear the words of your handmaid." He answered, "I do hear."

title: 2 Samuel 20:18
text: Then she spoke, saying, "They were used to say in old times, 'They shall surely ask counsel at Abel;' and so they settled it.

title: 2 Samuel 20:19
text: I am among those who are peaceable and faithful in Israel. You seek to destroy a city and a mother in Israel. Why will you swallow up the inheritance of Yahweh?"

title: 2 Samuel 20:20
text: Joab answered, "Far be it, far be it from me, that I should swallow up or destroy.

title: 2 Samuel 20:21
text: The matter is not so. But a man of the hill country of Ephraim, Sheba the son of Bichri by name, has lifted up his hand against the king, even against David. Deliver him only, and I will depart from the city." The woman said to Joab, "Behold, his head shall be thrown to you over the wall."

title: 2 Samuel 20:22
text: Then the woman went to all the people in her wisdom. They cut off the head of Sheba the son of Bichri, and threw it out to Joab. He blew the trumpet, and they were dispersed from the city, every man to his tent. Joab returned to Jerusalem to the king.

title: 2 Samuel 20:23
text: Now Joab was over all the army of Israel; and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was over the Cherethites and over the Pelethites;

title: 2 Samuel 20:24
text: and Adoram was over the men subject to forced labor; and Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud was the recorder;

title: 2 Samuel 20:25
text: and Sheva was scribe; and Zadok and Abiathar were priests;

title: 2 Samuel 20:26
text: and also Ira the Jairite was chief minister to David.

title: 2 Samuel 21:1
text: There was a famine in the days of David three years, year after year; and David sought the face of Yahweh. Yahweh said, "It is for Saul, and for his bloody house, because he put to death the Gibeonites."

title: 2 Samuel 21:2
text: The king called the Gibeonites, and said to them (now the Gibeonites were not of the children of Israel, but of the remnant of the Amorites; and the children of Israel had sworn to them: and Saul sought to kill them in his zeal for the children of Israel and Judah);

title: 2 Samuel 21:3
text: and David said to the Gibeonites, "What shall I do for you? And with what shall I make atonement, that you may bless the inheritance of Yahweh?"

title: 2 Samuel 21:4
text: The Gibeonites said to him, "It is no matter of silver or gold between us and Saul, or his house; neither is it for us to put any man to death in Israel." He said, "Whatever you say, that will I do for you."

title: 2 Samuel 21:5
text: They said to the king, "The man who consumed us, and who devised against us, that we should be destroyed from remaining in any of the borders of Israel,

title: 2 Samuel 21:6
text: let seven men of his sons be delivered to us, and we will hang them up to Yahweh in Gibeah of Saul, the chosen of Yahweh." The king said, "I will give them."

title: 2 Samuel 21:7
text: But the king spared Mephibosheth, the son of Jonathan the son of Saul, because of Yahweh's oath that was between them, between David and Jonathan the son of Saul.

title: 2 Samuel 21:8
text: But the king took the two sons of Rizpah the daughter of Aiah, whom she bore to Saul, Armoni and Mephibosheth; and the five sons of Michal the daughter of Saul, whom she bore to Adriel the son of Barzillai the Meholathite.

title: 2 Samuel 21:9
text: He delivered them into the hands of the Gibeonites, and they hanged them in the mountain before Yahweh, and all seven of them fell together. They were put to death in the days of harvest, in the first days, at the beginning of barley harvest.

title: 2 Samuel 21:10
text: Rizpah the daughter of Aiah took sackcloth, and spread it for her on the rock, from the beginning of harvest until water was poured on them from the sky. She allowed neither the birds of the sky to rest on them by day, nor the animals of the field by night.

title: 2 Samuel 21:11
text: It was told David what Rizpah the daughter of Aiah, the concubine of Saul, had done.

title: 2 Samuel 21:12
text: David went and took the bones of Saul and the bones of Jonathan his son from the men of Jabesh Gilead, who had stolen them from the street of Beth Shan, where the Philistines had hanged them, in the day that the Philistines killed Saul in Gilboa;

title: 2 Samuel 21:13
text: and he brought up from there the bones of Saul and the bones of Jonathan his son: and they gathered the bones of those who were hanged.

title: 2 Samuel 21:14
text: They buried the bones of Saul and Jonathan his son in the country of Benjamin in Zela, in the tomb of Kish his father: and they performed all that the king commanded. After that God was entreated for the land.

title: 2 Samuel 21:15
text: The Philistines had war again with Israel; and David went down, and his servants with him, and fought against the Philistines. David grew faint;

title: 2 Samuel 21:16
text: and Ishbibenob, who was of the sons of the giant, the weight of whose spear was three hundred [shekels] of brass in weight, he being armed with a new [sword], thought to have slain David.

title: 2 Samuel 21:17
text: But Abishai the son of Zeruiah helped him, and struck the Philistine, and killed him. Then the men of David swore to him, saying, "You shall go no more out with us to battle, that you don't quench the lamp of Israel."

title: 2 Samuel 21:18
text: It came to pass after this, that there was again war with the Philistines at Gob: then Sibbecai the Hushathite killed Saph, who was of the sons of the giant.

title: 2 Samuel 21:19
text: There was again war with the Philistines at Gob; and Elhanan the son of Jaareoregim the Bethlehemite killed Goliath the Gittite's brother, the staff of whose spear was like a weaver's beam.

title: 2 Samuel 21:20
text: There was again war at Gath, where there was a man of great stature, who had on every hand six fingers, and on every foot six toes, four and twenty in number; and he also was born to the giant.

title: 2 Samuel 21:21
text: When he defied Israel, Jonathan the son of Shimei, David's brother, killed him.

title: 2 Samuel 21:22
text: These four were born to the giant in Gath; and they fell by the hand of David, and by the hand of his servants.

title: 2 Samuel 22:1
text: David spoke to Yahweh the words of this song in the day that Yahweh delivered him out of the hand of all his enemies, and out of the hand of Saul:

title: 2 Samuel 22:2
text: and he said, "Yahweh is my rock, my fortress, and my deliverer, even mine;

title: 2 Samuel 22:3
text: God, my rock, in him I will take refuge; my shield, and the horn of my salvation, my high tower, and my refuge. My savior, you save me from violence.

title: 2 Samuel 22:4
text: I will call on Yahweh, who is worthy to be praised: So shall I be saved from my enemies.

title: 2 Samuel 22:5
text: For the waves of death surrounded me. The floods of ungodliness made me afraid.

title: 2 Samuel 22:6
text: The cords of Sheol were around me. The snares of death caught me.

title: 2 Samuel 22:7
text: In my distress I called on Yahweh. Yes, I called to my God. He heard my voice out of his temple. My cry [came] into his ears.

title: 2 Samuel 22:8
text: Then the earth shook and trembled. The foundations of heaven quaked and were shaken, because he was angry.

title: 2 Samuel 22:9
text: Smoke went up out of his nostrils. Fire out of his mouth devoured. Coals were kindled by it.

title: 2 Samuel 22:10
text: He bowed the heavens also, and came down. Thick darkness was under his feet.

title: 2 Samuel 22:11
text: He rode on a cherub, and flew. Yes, he was seen on the wings of the wind.

title: 2 Samuel 22:12
text: He made darkness pavilions around himself: gathering of waters, and thick clouds of the skies.

title: 2 Samuel 22:13
text: At the brightness before him, coals of fire were kindled.

title: 2 Samuel 22:14
text: Yahweh thundered from heaven. The Most High uttered his voice.

title: 2 Samuel 22:15
text: He sent out arrows, and scattered them; lightning, and confused them.

title: 2 Samuel 22:16
text: Then the channels of the sea appeared. The foundations of the world were laid bare by the rebuke of Yahweh, At the blast of the breath of his nostrils.

title: 2 Samuel 22:17
text: He sent from on high and he took me. He drew me out of many waters.

title: 2 Samuel 22:18
text: He delivered me from my strong enemy, from those who hated me, for they were too mighty for me.

title: 2 Samuel 22:19
text: They came on me in the day of my calamity, but Yahweh was my support.

title: 2 Samuel 22:20
text: He also brought me out into a large place. He delivered me, because he delighted in me.

title: 2 Samuel 22:21
text: Yahweh rewarded me according to my righteousness. He rewarded me according to the cleanness of my hands.

title: 2 Samuel 22:22
text: For I have kept the ways of Yahweh, and have not wickedly departed from my God.

title: 2 Samuel 22:23
text: For all his ordinances were before me. As for his statutes, I did not depart from them.

title: 2 Samuel 22:24
text: I was also perfect toward him. I kept myself from my iniquity.

title: 2 Samuel 22:25
text: Therefore Yahweh has rewarded me according to my righteousness, According to my cleanness in his eyesight.

title: 2 Samuel 22:26
text: With the merciful you will show yourself merciful. With the perfect man you will show yourself perfect.

title: 2 Samuel 22:27
text: With the pure you will show yourself pure. With the crooked you will show yourself shrewd.

title: 2 Samuel 22:28
text: You will save the afflicted people, But your eyes are on the haughty, that you may bring them down.

title: 2 Samuel 22:29
text: For you are my lamp, Yahweh. Yahweh will light up my darkness.

title: 2 Samuel 22:30
text: For by you, I run against a troop. By my God, I leap over a wall.

title: 2 Samuel 22:31
text: As for God, his way is perfect. The word of Yahweh is tested. He is a shield to all those who take refuge in him.

title: 2 Samuel 22:32
text: For who is God, besides Yahweh? Who is a rock, besides our God?

title: 2 Samuel 22:33
text: God is my strong fortress. He makes my way perfect.

title: 2 Samuel 22:34
text: He makes his feet like hinds' [feet], and sets me on my high places.

title: 2 Samuel 22:35
text: He teaches my hands to war, so that my arms bend a bow of brass.

title: 2 Samuel 22:36
text: You have also given me the shield of your salvation. Your gentleness has made me great.

title: 2 Samuel 22:37
text: You have enlarged my steps under me. My feet have not slipped.

title: 2 Samuel 22:38
text: I have pursued my enemies and destroyed them. I didn't turn again until they were consumed.

title: 2 Samuel 22:39
text: I have consumed them, and struck them through, so that they can't arise. Yes, they have fallen under my feet.

title: 2 Samuel 22:40
text: For you have armed me with strength for the battle. You have subdued under me those who rose up against me.

title: 2 Samuel 22:41
text: You have also made my enemies turn their backs to me, that I might cut off those who hate me.

title: 2 Samuel 22:42
text: They looked, but there was none to save; even to Yahweh, but he didn't answer them.

title: 2 Samuel 22:43
text: Then I beat them as small as the dust of the earth. I crushed them as the mire of the streets, and spread them abroad.

title: 2 Samuel 22:44
text: You also have delivered me from the strivings of my people. You have kept me to be the head of the nations. A people whom I have not known will serve me.

title: 2 Samuel 22:45
text: The foreigners will submit themselves to me. As soon as they hear of me, they will obey me.

title: 2 Samuel 22:46
text: The foreigners will fade away, and will come trembling out of their close places.

title: 2 Samuel 22:47
text: Yahweh lives! Blessed be my rock! Exalted be God, the rock of my salvation,

title: 2 Samuel 22:48
text: even the God who executes vengeance for me, who brings down peoples under me,

title: 2 Samuel 22:49
text: who brings me away from my enemies. Yes, you lift me up above those who rise up against me. You deliver me from the violent man.

title: 2 Samuel 22:50
text: Therefore I will give thanks to you, Yahweh, among the nations. Will sing praises to your name.

title: 2 Samuel 22:51
text: He gives great deliverance to his king, and shows loving kindness to his anointed, to David and to his seed, forevermore."

title: 2 Samuel 23:1
text: Now these are the last words of David. David the son of Jesse says, the man who was raised on high says, the anointed of the God of Jacob, the sweet psalmist of Israel:

title: 2 Samuel 23:2
text: "The Spirit of Yahweh spoke by me. His word was on my tongue.

title: 2 Samuel 23:3
text: The God of Israel said, the Rock of Israel spoke to me, 'One who rules over men righteously, who rules in the fear of God,

title: 2 Samuel 23:4
text: shall be as the light of the morning, when the sun rises, a morning without clouds, when the tender grass springs out of the earth, through clear shining after rain.'

title: 2 Samuel 23:5
text: Most certainly my house is not so with God, yet he has made with me an everlasting covenant, ordered in all things, and sure, for it is all my salvation, and all [my] desire, although he doesn't make it grow.

title: 2 Samuel 23:6
text: But all of the ungodly shall be as thorns to be thrust away, because they can't be taken with the hand,

title: 2 Samuel 23:7
text: But the man who touches them must be armed with iron and the staff of a spear. They shall be utterly burned with fire in their place."

title: 2 Samuel 23:8
text: These are the names of the mighty men whom David had: Josheb Basshebeth a Tahchemonite, chief of the captains; the same was Adino the Eznite, against eight hundred slain at one time.

title: 2 Samuel 23:9
text: After him was Eleazar the son of Dodai the son of an Ahohite, one of the three mighty men with David, when they defied the Philistines who were there gathered together to battle, and the men of Israel were gone away.

title: 2 Samuel 23:10
text: He arose, and struck the Philistines until his hand was weary, and his hand froze to the sword; and Yahweh worked a great victory that day; and the people returned after him only to take spoil.

title: 2 Samuel 23:11
