text: The couriers went forth in haste by the king's commandment, and the decree was given out in the citadel of Susa. The king and Haman sat down to drink; but the city of Shushan was perplexed.

title: Esther 4:1
text: Now when Mordecai found out all that was done, Mordecai tore his clothes, and put on sackcloth with ashes, and went out into the midst of the city, and wailed loudly and a bitterly.

title: Esther 4:2
text: He came even before the king's gate, for no one is allowed inside the king's gate clothed with sackcloth.

title: Esther 4:3
text: In every province, wherever the king's commandment and his decree came, there was great mourning among the Jews, and fasting, and weeping, and wailing; and many lay in sackcloth and ashes.

title: Esther 4:4
text: Esther's maidens and her eunuchs came and told her this, and the queen was exceedingly grieved. She sent clothing to Mordecai, to replace his sackcloth; but he didn't receive it.

title: Esther 4:5
text: Then Esther called for Hathach, one of the king's eunuchs, whom he had appointed to attend her, and commanded him to go to Mordecai, to find out what this was, and why it was.

title: Esther 4:6
text: So Hathach went out to Mordecai, to city square which was before the king's gate.

title: Esther 4:7
text: Mordecai told him of all that had happened to him, and the exact sum of the money that Haman had promised to pay to the king's treasuries for the destruction of the Jews.

title: Esther 4:8
text: He also gave him the copy of the writing of the decree that was given out in Shushan to destroy them, to show it to Esther, and to declare it to her, and to urge her to go in to the king, to make supplication to him, and to make request before him, for her people.

title: Esther 4:9
text: Hathach came and told Esther the words of Mordecai.

title: Esther 4:10
text: Then Esther spoke to Hathach, and gave him a message to Mordecai:

title: Esther 4:11
text: "All the king's servants, and the people of the king's provinces, know, that whoever, whether man or woman, comes to the king into the inner court without being called, there is one law for him, that he be put to death, except those to whom the king might hold out the golden scepter, that he may live. I have not been called to come in to the king these thirty days."

title: Esther 4:12
text: They told to Mordecai Esther's words.

title: Esther 4:13
text: Then Mordecai asked them return answer to Esther, "Don't think to yourself that you will escape in the king's house any more than all the Jews.

title: Esther 4:14
text: For if you remain silent now, then relief and deliverance will come to the Jews from another place, but you and your father's house will perish. Who knows if you haven't come to the kingdom for such a time as this?"

title: Esther 4:15
text: Then Esther asked them to answer Mordecai,

title: Esther 4:16
text: "Go, gather together all the Jews who are present in Shushan, and fast for me, and neither eat nor drink three days, night or day. I and my maidens will also fast the same way. Then I will go in to the king, which is against the law; and if I perish, I perish."

title: Esther 4:17
text: So Mordecai went his way, and did according to all that Esther had commanded him.

title: Esther 5:1
text: Now it happened on the third day that Esther put on her royal clothing, and stood in the inner court of the king's house, next to the king's house. The king sat on his royal throne in the royal house, next to the entrance of the house.

title: Esther 5:2
text: When the king saw Esther the queen standing in the court, she obtained favor in his sight; and the king held out to Esther the golden scepter that was in his hand. So Esther came near, and touched the top of the scepter.

title: Esther 5:3
text: Then the king asked her, "What would you like, queen Esther? What is your request? It shall be given you even to the half of the kingdom."

title: Esther 5:4
text: Esther said, "If it seems good to the king, let the king and Haman come today to the banquet that I have prepared for him."

title: Esther 5:5
text: Then the king said, "Bring Haman quickly, so that it may be done as Esther has said." So the king and Haman came to the banquet that Esther had prepared.

title: Esther 5:6
text: The king said to Esther at the banquet of wine, "What is your petition? It shall be granted you. What is your request? Even to the half of the kingdom it shall be performed."

title: Esther 5:7
text: Then Esther answered and said, "My petition and my request is this.

title: Esther 5:8
text: If I have found favor in the sight of the king, and if it please the king to grant my petition and to perform my request, let the king and Haman come to the banquet that I will prepare for them, and I will do tomorrow as the king has said."

title: Esther 5:9
text: Then Haman went out that day joyful and glad of heart, but when Haman saw Mordecai in the king's gate, that he didn't stand up nor move for him, he was filled with wrath against Mordecai.

title: Esther 5:10
text: Nevertheless Haman restrained himself, and went home. There, he sent and called for his friends and Zeresh his wife.

title: Esther 5:11
text: Haman recounted to them the glory of his riches, the multitude of his children, all the things in which the king had promoted him, and how he had advanced him above the princes and servants of the king.

title: Esther 5:12
text: Haman also said, "Yes, Esther the queen let no man come in with the king to the banquet that she had prepared but myself; and tomorrow I am also invited by her together with the king.

title: Esther 5:13
text: Yet all this avails me nothing, so long as I see Mordecai the Jew sitting at the king's gate."

title: Esther 5:14
text: Then Zeresh his wife and all his friends said to him, "Let a gallows be made fifty cubits high, and in the morning speak to the king about hanging Mordecai on it. Then go in merrily with the king to the banquet." This pleased Haman, so he had the gallows made.

title: Esther 6:1
text: On that night, the king couldn't sleep. He commanded the book of records of the chronicles to be brought, and they were read to the king.

title: Esther 6:2
text: It was found written that Mordecai had told of Bigthana and Teresh, two of the king's eunuchs, who were doorkeepers, who had tried to lay hands on the King Ahasuerus.

title: Esther 6:3
text: The king said, "What honor and dignity has been bestowed on Mordecai for this?" Then the king's servants who attended him said, "Nothing has been done for him."

title: Esther 6:4
text: The king said, "Who is in the court?" Now Haman had come into the outer court of the king's house, to speak to the king about hanging Mordecai on the gallows that he had prepared for him.

title: Esther 6:5
text: The king's servants said to him, "Behold, Haman stands in the court." The king said, "Let him come in."

title: Esther 6:6
text: So Haman came in. The king said to him, "What shall be done to the man whom the king delights to honor?" Now Haman said in his heart, "Who would the king delight to honor more than myself?"

title: Esther 6:7
text: Haman said to the king, "For the man whom the king delights to honor,

title: Esther 6:8
text: let royal clothing be brought which the king uses to wear, and the horse that the king rides on, and on the head of which a crown royal is set.

title: Esther 6:9
text: Let the clothing and the horse be delivered to the hand of one of the king's most noble princes, that they may array the man whom the king delights to honor with them, and have him ride on horseback through the city square, and proclaim before him, 'Thus shall it be done to the man whom the king delights to honor!'"

title: Esther 6:10
text: Then the king said to Haman, "Hurry and take the clothing and the horse, as you have said, and do this for Mordecai the Jew, who sits at the king's gate. Let nothing fail of all that you have spoken."

title: Esther 6:11
text: Then Haman took the clothing and the horse, and arrayed Mordecai, and had him ride through the city square, and proclaimed before him, "Thus shall it be done to the man whom the king delights to honor!"

title: Esther 6:12
text: Mordecai came back to the king's gate, but Haman hurried to his house, mourning and having his head covered.

title: Esther 6:13
text: Haman recounted to Zeresh his wife and all his friends everything that had happened to him. Then his wise men and Zeresh his wife said to him, "If Mordecai, before whom you have begun to fall, is of Jewish descent, you will not prevail against him, but you will surely fall before him."

title: Esther 6:14
text: While they were yet talking with him, the king's eunuchs came, and hurried to bring Haman to the banquet that Esther had prepared.

title: Esther 7:1
text: So the king and Haman came to banquet with Esther the queen.

title: Esther 7:2
text: The king said again to Esther on the second day at the banquet of wine, "What is your petition, queen Esther? It shall be granted you. What is your request? Even to the half of the kingdom it shall be performed."

title: Esther 7:3
text: Then Esther the queen answered, "If I have found favor in your sight, O king, and if it please the king, let my life be given me at my petition, and my people at my request.

title: Esther 7:4
text: For we are sold, I and my people, to be destroyed, to be slain, and to perish. But if we had been sold for bondservants and bondmaids, I would have held my peace, although the adversary could not have compensated for the king's loss."

title: Esther 7:5
text: Then King Ahasuerus said to Esther the queen, "Who is he, and where is he who dared presume in his heart to do so?"

title: Esther 7:6
text: Esther said, "An adversary and an enemy, even this wicked Haman!" Then Haman was afraid before the king and the queen.

title: Esther 7:7
text: The king arose in his wrath from the banquet of wine and went into the palace garden. Haman stood up to make request for his life to Esther the queen; for he saw that there was evil determined against him by the king.

title: Esther 7:8
text: Then the king returned out of the palace garden into the place of the banquet of wine; and Haman had fallen on the couch where Esther was. Then the king said, "Will he even assault the queen in front of me in the house?" As the word went out of the king's mouth, they covered Haman's face.

title: Esther 7:9
text: Then Harbonah, one of the eunuchs who were with the king said, "Behold, the gallows fifty cubits high, which Haman has made for Mordecai, who spoke good for the king, is standing at Haman's house." The king said, "Hang him on it!"

title: Esther 7:10
text: So they hanged Haman on the gallows that he had prepared for Mordecai. Then was the king's wrath pacified.

title: Esther 8:1
text: On that day, King Ahasuerus gave the house of Haman, the Jews' enemy, to Esther the queen. Mordecai came before the king; for Esther had told what he was to her.

title: Esther 8:2
text: The king took off his ring, which he had taken from Haman, and gave it to Mordecai. Esther set Mordecai over the house of Haman.

title: Esther 8:3
text: Esther spoke yet again before the king, and fell down at his feet, and begged him with tears to put away the mischief of Haman the Agagite, and his device that he had devised against the Jews.

title: Esther 8:4
text: Then the king held out to Esther the golden scepter. So Esther arose, and stood before the king.

title: Esther 8:5
text: She said, "If it pleases the king, and if I have found favor in his sight, and the thing seem right to the king, and I am pleasing in his eyes, let it be written to reverse the letters devised by Haman, the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, which he wrote to destroy the Jews who are in all the king's provinces.

title: Esther 8:6
text: For how can I endure to see the evil that would come to my people? How can I endure to see the destruction of my relatives?"

title: Esther 8:7
text: Then King Ahasuerus said to Esther the queen and to Mordecai the Jew, "See, I have given Esther the house of Haman, and him they have hanged on the gallows, because he laid his hand on the Jews.

title: Esther 8:8
text: Write also to the Jews, as it pleases you, in the king's name, and seal it with the king's ring; for the writing which is written in the king's name, and sealed with the king's ring, may not be reversed by any man."

title: Esther 8:9
text: Then the king's scribes were called at that time, in the third month Sivan, on the twenty-third day of the month; and it was written according to all that Mordecai commanded to the Jews, and to the satraps, and the governors and princes of the provinces which are from India to Ethiopia, one hundred twenty-seven provinces, to every province according to its writing, and to every people in their language, and to the Jews in their writing, and in their language.

title: Esther 8:10
text: He wrote in the name of King Ahasuerus, and sealed it with the king's ring, and sent letters by courier on horseback, riding on royal horses that were bread from swift steeds.

title: Esther 8:11
text: In those letters, the king granted the Jews who were in every city to gather themselves together, and to defend their life, to destroy, to kill, and to cause to perish, all the power of the people and province that would assault them, their little ones and women, and to plunder their possessions,

title: Esther 8:12
text: on one day in all the provinces of King Ahasuerus, on the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, which is the month Adar.

title: Esther 8:13
text: A copy of the letter, that the decree should be given out in every province, was published to all the peoples, that the Jews should be ready for that day to avenge themselves on their enemies.

title: Esther 8:14
text: So the couriers who rode on royal horses went out, hastened and pressed on by the king's commandment. The decree was given out in the citadel of Susa.

title: Esther 8:15
text: Mordecai went out of the presence of the king in royal clothing of blue and white, and with a great crown of gold, and with a robe of fine linen and purple; and the city of Susa shouted and was glad.

title: Esther 8:16
text: The Jews had light, gladness, joy, and honor.

title: Esther 8:17
text: In every province, and in every city, wherever the king's commandment and his decree came, the Jews had gladness, joy, a feast, and a good day. Many from among the peoples of the land became Jews; for the fear of the Jews was fallen on them.

title: Esther 9:1
text: Now in the twelfth month, which is the month Adar, on the thirteenth day of the month, when the king's commandment and his decree drew near to be put in execution, on the day that the enemies of the Jews hoped to conquer them, (but it was turned out the opposite happened, that the Jews conquered those who hated them),

title: Esther 9:2
text: the Jews gathered themselves together in their cities throughout all the provinces of the King Ahasuerus, to lay hands on those who wanted to harm them. No one could withstand them, because the fear of them had fallen on all the people.

title: Esther 9:3
text: All the princes of the provinces, the satraps, the governors, and those who did the king's business helped the Jews, because the fear of Mordecai had fallen on them.

title: Esther 9:4
text: For Mordecai was great in the king's house, and his fame went out throughout all the provinces; for the man Mordecai grew greater and greater.

title: Esther 9:5
text: The Jews struck all their enemies with the stroke of the sword, and with slaughter and destruction, and did what they wanted to those who hated them.

title: Esther 9:6
text: In the citadel of Susa, the Jews killed and destroyed five hundred men.

title: Esther 9:7
text: They killed Parshandatha, Dalphon, Aspatha,

title: Esther 9:8
text: Poratha, Adalia, Aridatha,

title: Esther 9:9
text: Parmashta, Arisai, Aridai, and Vaizatha,

title: Esther 9:10
text: the ten sons of Haman the son of Hammedatha, the Jew's enemy, but they didn't lay their hand on the plunder.

title: Esther 9:11
text: On that day, the number of those who were slain in the citadel of Susa was brought before the king.

title: Esther 9:12
text: The king said to Esther the queen, "The Jews have slain and destroyed five hundred men in the citadel of Susa, including the ten sons of Haman; what then have they done in the rest of the king's provinces! Now what is your petition? It shall be granted you. What is your further request? It shall be done."

title: Esther 9:13
text: Then Esther said, "If it pleases the king, let it be granted to the Jews who are in Shushan to do tomorrow also according to this day's decree, and let Haman's ten sons be hanged on the gallows."

title: Esther 9:14
text: The king commanded this to be done. A decree was given out in Shushan; and they hanged Haman's ten sons.

title: Esther 9:15
text: The Jews who were in Shushan gathered themselves together on the fourteenth day also of the month Adar, and killed three hundred men in Shushan; but they didn't lay their hand on the spoil.

title: Esther 9:16
text: The other Jews who were in the king's provinces gathered themselves together, defended their lives, had rest from their enemies, and killed seventy-five thousand of those who hated them; but they didn't lay their hand on the plunder.

title: Esther 9:17
text: This was done on the thirteenth day of the month Adar; and on the fourteenth day of that month they rested and made it a day of feasting and gladness.

title: Esther 9:18
text: But the Jews who were in Shushan assembled together on the thirteenth and on the fourteenth days of the month; and on the fifteenth day of that month, they rested, and made it a day of feasting and gladness.

title: Esther 9:19
text: Therefore the Jews of the villages, who live in the unwalled towns, make the fourteenth day of the month Adar a day of gladness and feasting, a good day, and a day of sending presents of food to one another.

title: Esther 9:20
text: Mordecai wrote these things, and sent letters to all the Jews who were in all the provinces of the king Ahasuerus, both near and far,

title: Esther 9:21
text: to enjoin them that they should keep the fourteenth and fifteenth days of the month Adar yearly,

title: Esther 9:22
text: as the days in which the Jews had rest from their enemies, and the month which was turned to them from sorrow to gladness, and from mourning into a good day; that they should make them days of feasting and gladness, and of sending presents of food to one another, and gifts to the needy.

title: Esther 9:23
text: The Jews accepted the custom that they had begun, as Mordecai had written to them;

title: Esther 9:24
text: because Haman the son of Hammedatha, the Agagite, the enemy of all the Jews, had plotted against the Jews to destroy them, and had cast "Pur," that is the lot, to consume them, and to destroy them;

title: Esther 9:25
text: but when this became known to the king, he commanded by letters that his wicked device, which he had devised against the Jews, should return on his own head, and that he and his sons should be hanged on the gallows.

title: Esther 9:26
text: Therefore they called these days "Purim," from the word "Pur." Therefore because of all the words of this letter, and of that which they had seen concerning this matter, and that which had come to them,

title: Esther 9:27
text: the Jews established, and imposed on themselves, and on their descendants, and on all those who joined themselves to them, so that it should not fail, that they would keep these two days according to what was written, and according to its appointed time, every year;

title: Esther 9:28
text: and that these days should be remembered and kept throughout every generation, every family, every province, and every city; and that these days of Purim should not fail from among the Jews, nor the memory of them perish from their seed.

title: Esther 9:29
text: Then Esther the queen, the daughter of Abihail, and Mordecai the Jew, wrote with all authority to confirm this second letter of Purim.

title: Esther 9:30
text: He sent letters to all the Jews, to the hundred twenty-seven provinces of the kingdom of Ahasuerus, with words of peace and truth,

title: Esther 9:31
text: to confirm these days of Purim in their appointed times, as Mordecai the Jew and Esther the queen had decreed, and as they had imposed upon themselves and their descendants, in the matter of the fastings and their cry.

title: Esther 9:32
text: The commandment of Esther confirmed these matters of Purim; and it was written in the book.

title: Esther 10:1
text: King Ahasuerus laid a tribute on the land, and on the islands of the sea.

title: Esther 10:2
text: All the acts of his power and of his might, and the full account of the greatness of Mordecai, to which the king advanced him, aren't they written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Media and Persia?

title: Esther 10:3
text: For Mordecai the Jew was next to King Ahasuerus, and great among the Jews, and accepted by the multitude of his brothers, seeking the good of his people, and speaking peace to all his descendants.

title: Job 1:1
text: There was a man in the land of Uz, whose name was Job. That man was blameless and upright, and one who feared God, and turned away from evil.

title: Job 1:2
text: There were born to him seven sons and three daughters.

title: Job 1:3
text: His possessions also were seven thousand sheep, three thousand camels, five hundred yoke of oxen, five hundred female donkeys, and a very great household; so that this man was the greatest of all the children of the east.

title: Job 1:4
text: His sons went and held a feast in the house of each one on his birthday; and they sent and called for their three sisters to eat and to drink with them.

title: Job 1:5
text: It was so, when the days of their feasting had run their course, that Job sent and sanctified them, and rose up early in the morning, and offered burnt offerings according to the number of them all. For Job said, "It may be that my sons have sinned, and renounced God in their hearts." Job did so continually.

title: Job 1:6
text: Now it happened on the day when God's sons came to present themselves before Yahweh, that Satan also came among them.

title: Job 1:7
text: Yahweh said to Satan, "Where have you come from?" Then Satan answered Yahweh, and said, "From going back and forth in the earth, and from walking up and down in it."

title: Job 1:8
text: Yahweh said to Satan, "Have you considered my servant, Job? For there is none like him in the earth, a blameless and an upright man, one who fears God, and turns away from evil."

title: Job 1:9
text: Then Satan answered Yahweh, and said, "Does Job fear God for nothing?

title: Job 1:10
text: Haven't you made a hedge around him, and around his house, and around all that he has, on every side? You have blessed the work of his hands, and his substance is increased in the land.

title: Job 1:11
text: But put forth your hand now, and touch all that he has, and he will renounce you to your face."

title: Job 1:12
text: Yahweh said to Satan, "Behold, all that he has is in your power. Only on himself don't put forth your hand." So Satan went forth from the presence of Yahweh.

title: Job 1:13
text: It fell on a day when his sons and his daughters were eating and drinking wine in their eldest brother's house,

title: Job 1:14
text: that there came a messenger to Job, and said, "The oxen were plowing, and the donkeys feeding beside them,

title: Job 1:15
text: and the Sabeans attacked, and took them away. Yes, they have killed the servants with the edge of the sword, and I alone have escaped to tell you."

title: Job 1:16
text: While he was still speaking, there also came another, and said, "The fire of God has fallen from the sky, and has burned up the sheep and the servants, and consumed them, and I alone have escaped to tell you."

title: Job 1:17
text: While he was still speaking, there came also another, and said, "The Chaldeans made three bands, and swept down on the camels, and have taken them away, yes, and killed the servants with the edge of the sword; and I alone have escaped to tell you."

title: Job 1:18
text: While he was still speaking, there came also another, and said, "Your sons and your daughters were eating and drinking wine in their eldest brother's house,

title: Job 1:19
text: and behold, there came a great wind from the wilderness, and struck the four corners of the house, and it fell on the young men, and they are dead. I alone have escaped to tell you."

title: Job 1:20
text: Then Job arose, and tore his robe, and shaved his head, and fell down on the ground, and worshiped.

title: Job 1:21
text: He said, "Naked I came out of my mother's womb, and naked shall I return there. Yahweh gave, and Yahweh has taken away. Blessed be the name of Yahweh."

title: Job 1:22
text: In all this, Job did not sin, nor charge God with wrongdoing.

title: Job 2:1
text: Again it happened on the day when the God's sons came to present themselves before Yahweh, that Satan came also among them to present himself before Yahweh.

title: Job 2:2
text: Yahweh said to Satan, "Where have you come from?" Satan answered Yahweh, and said, "From going back and forth in the earth, and from walking up and down in it."

title: Job 2:3
text: Yahweh said to Satan, "Have you considered my servant Job? For there is none like him in the earth, a blameless and an upright man, one who fears God, and turns away from evil. He still maintains his integrity, although you incited me against him, to ruin him without cause."

title: Job 2:4
text: Satan answered Yahweh, and said, "Skin for skin. Yes, all that a man has he will give for his life.

title: Job 2:5
text: But put forth your hand now, and touch his bone and his flesh, and he will renounce you to your face."

title: Job 2:6
text: Yahweh said to Satan, "Behold, he is in your hand. Only spare his life."

title: Job 2:7
text: So Satan went forth from the presence of Yahweh, and struck Job with painful sores from the sole of his foot to his head.

title: Job 2:8
text: He took for himself a potsherd to scrape himself with, and he sat among the ashes.

title: Job 2:9
text: Then his wife said to him, "Do you still maintain your integrity? Renounce God, and die."

title: Job 2:10
text: But he said to her, "You speak as one of the foolish women would speak. What? Shall we receive good at the hand of God, and shall we not receive evil?" In all this Job didn't sin with his lips.

title: Job 2:11
text: Now when Job's three friends heard of all this evil that had come on him, they each came from his own place: Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite, and they made an appointment together to come to sympathize with him and to comfort him.

title: Job 2:12
text: When they lifted up their eyes from a distance, and didn't recognize him, they raised their voices, and wept; and they each tore his robe, and sprinkled dust on their heads toward the sky.

title: Job 2:13
text: So they sat down with him on the ground seven days and seven nights, and none spoke a word to him, for they saw that his grief was very great.

title: Job 3:1
text: After this Job opened his mouth, and cursed the day of his birth.

title: Job 3:2
text: Job answered:

title: Job 3:3
text: "Let the day perish in which I was born, the night which said, 'There is a boy conceived.'

title: Job 3:4
text: Let that day be darkness. Don't let God from above seek for it, neither let the light shine on it.

title: Job 3:5
text: Let darkness and the shadow of death claim it for their own. Let a cloud dwell on it. Let all that makes black the day terrify it.

title: Job 3:6
text: As for that night, let thick darkness seize on it. Let it not rejoice among the days of the year. Let it not come into the number of the months.

title: Job 3:7
text: Behold, let that night be barren. Let no joyful voice come therein.

title: Job 3:8
text: Let them curse it who curse the day, who are ready to rouse up leviathan.

title: Job 3:9
text: Let the stars of its twilight be dark. Let it look for light, but have none, neither let it see the eyelids of the morning,

title: Job 3:10
text: because it didn't shut up the doors of my mother's womb, nor did it hide trouble from my eyes.

title: Job 3:11
text: "Why didn't I die from the womb? Why didn't I give up the spirit when my mother bore me?

title: Job 3:12
text: Why did the knees receive me? Or why the breast, that I should nurse?

title: Job 3:13
text: For now should I have lain down and been quiet. I should have slept, then I would have been at rest,

title: Job 3:14
text: with kings and counselors of the earth, who built up waste places for themselves;

title: Job 3:15
text: or with princes who had gold, who filled their houses with silver:

title: Job 3:16
text: or as a hidden untimely birth I had not been, as infants who never saw light.

title: Job 3:17
text: There the wicked cease from troubling. There the weary are at rest.

title: Job 3:18
text: There the prisoners are at ease together. They don't hear the voice of the taskmaster.

title: Job 3:19
text: The small and the great are there. The servant is free from his master.

title: Job 3:20
text: "Why is light given to him who is in misery, life to the bitter in soul,

title: Job 3:21
text: Who long for death, but it doesn't come; and dig for it more than for hidden treasures,

title: Job 3:22
text: who rejoice exceedingly, and are glad, when they can find the grave?

title: Job 3:23
text: Why is light given to a man whose way is hidden, whom God has hedged in?

title: Job 3:24
text: For my sighing comes before I eat. My groanings are poured out like water.

title: Job 3:25
text: For the thing which I fear comes on me, That which I am afraid of comes to me.

title: Job 3:26
text: I am not at ease, neither am I quiet, neither have I rest; but trouble comes."

title: Job 4:1
text: Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered,

title: Job 4:2
text: "If someone ventures to talk with you, will you be grieved? But who can withhold himself from speaking?

title: Job 4:3
text: Behold, you have instructed many, you have strengthened the weak hands.

title: Job 4:4
text: Your words have supported him who was falling, You have made firm the feeble knees.

title: Job 4:5
text: But now it is come to you, and you faint. It touches you, and you are troubled.

title: Job 4:6
text: Isn't your piety your confidence? Isn't the integrity of your ways your hope?

title: Job 4:7
text: "Remember, now, whoever perished, being innocent? Or where were the upright cut off?

title: Job 4:8
text: According to what I have seen, those who plow iniquity, and sow trouble, reap the same.

title: Job 4:9
text: By the breath of God they perish. By the blast of his anger are they consumed.

title: Job 4:10
text: The roaring of the lion, and the voice of the fierce lion, the teeth of the young lions, are broken.

title: Job 4:11
text: The old lion perishes for lack of prey. The cubs of the lioness are scattered abroad.

title: Job 4:12
text: "Now a thing was secretly brought to me. My ear received a whisper of it.

title: Job 4:13
text: In thoughts from the visions of the night, when deep sleep falls on men,

title: Job 4:14
text: fear came on me, and trembling, which made all my bones shake.

title: Job 4:15
text: Then a spirit passed before my face. The hair of my flesh stood up.

title: Job 4:16
text: It stood still, but I couldn't discern its appearance. A form was before my eyes. Silence, then I heard a voice, saying,

title: Job 4:17
text: 'Shall mortal man be more just than God? Shall a man be more pure than his Maker?

title: Job 4:18
text: Behold, he puts no trust in his servants. He charges his angels with error.

title: Job 4:19
text: How much more, those who dwell in houses of clay, whose foundation is in the dust, who are crushed before the moth!

title: Job 4:20
text: Between morning and evening they are destroyed. They perish forever without any regarding it.

title: Job 4:21
text: Isn't their tent cord plucked up within them? They die, and that without wisdom.'

title: Job 5:1
text: "Call now; is there any who will answer you? To which of the holy ones will you turn?

title: Job 5:2
text: For resentment kills the foolish man, and jealousy kills the simple.

title: Job 5:3
text: I have seen the foolish taking root, but suddenly I cursed his habitation.

title: Job 5:4
text: His children are far from safety. They are crushed in the gate. Neither is there any to deliver them,

title: Job 5:5
text: whose harvest the hungry eats up, and take it even out of the thorns. The snare gapes for their substance.

title: Job 5:6
text: For affliction doesn't come forth from the dust, neither does trouble spring out of the ground;

title: Job 5:7
text: but man is born to trouble, as the sparks fly upward.

title: Job 5:8
text: "But as for me, I would seek God. I would commit my cause to God,

title: Job 5:9
text: who does great things that can't be fathomed, marvelous things without number;

title: Job 5:10
text: who gives rain on the earth, and sends waters on the fields;

title: Job 5:11
text: so that he sets up on high those who are low, those who mourn are exalted to safety.

title: Job 5:12
text: He frustrates the devices of the crafty, So that their hands can't perform their enterprise.

title: Job 5:13
text: He takes the wise in their own craftiness; the counsel of the cunning is carried headlong.

title: Job 5:14
text: They meet with darkness in the day time, and grope at noonday as in the night.

title: Job 5:15
text: But he saves from the sword of their mouth, even the needy from the hand of the mighty.

title: Job 5:16
text: So the poor has hope, and injustice shuts her mouth.

title: Job 5:17
text: "Behold, happy is the man whom God corrects. Therefore do not despise the chastening of the Almighty.

title: Job 5:18
text: For he wounds, and binds up. He injures, and his hands make whole.

title: Job 5:19
text: He will deliver you in six troubles; yes, in seven no evil shall touch you.

title: Job 5:20
text: In famine he will redeem you from death; in war, from the power of the sword.

title: Job 5:21
text: You shall be hidden from the scourge of the tongue, neither shall you be afraid of destruction when it comes.

title: Job 5:22
text: At destruction and famine you shall laugh, neither shall you be afraid of the animals of the earth.

title: Job 5:23
text: For you shall be allied with the stones of the field. The animals of the field shall be at peace with you.

title: Job 5:24
text: You shall know that your tent is in peace. You shall visit your fold, and shall miss nothing.

title: Job 5:25
text: You shall know also that your seed shall be great, Your offspring as the grass of the earth.

title: Job 5:26
text: You shall come to your grave in a full age, like a shock of grain comes in its season.

title: Job 5:27
text: Look this, we have searched it, so it is. Hear it, and know it for your good."

title: Job 6:1
text: Then Job answered,

title: Job 6:2
text: "Oh that my anguish were weighed, and all my calamity laid in the balances!

title: Job 6:3
text: For now it would be heavier than the sand of the seas, therefore have my words been rash.

title: Job 6:4
text: For the arrows of the Almighty are within me. My spirit drinks up their poison. The terrors of God set themselves in array against me.

title: Job 6:5
text: Does the wild donkey bray when he has grass? Or does the ox low over his fodder?

title: Job 6:6
text: Can that which has no flavor be eaten without salt? Or is there any taste in the white of an egg?

title: Job 6:7
text: My soul refuses to touch them. They are as loathsome food to me.

title: Job 6:8
text: "Oh that I might have my request, that God would grant the thing that I long for,

title: Job 6:9
text: even that it would please God to crush me; that he would let loose his hand, and cut me off!

title: Job 6:10
text: Be it still my consolation, yes, let me exult in pain that doesn't spare, that I have not denied the words of the Holy One.

title: Job 6:11
text: What is my strength, that I should wait? What is my end, that I should be patient?

title: Job 6:12
text: Is my strength the strength of stones? Or is my flesh of brass?

title: Job 6:13
text: Isn't it that I have no help in me, That wisdom is driven quite from me?

title: Job 6:14
text: "To him who is ready to faint, kindness should be shown from his friend; even to him who forsakes the fear of the Almighty.

title: Job 6:15
text: My brothers have dealt deceitfully as a brook, as the channel of brooks that pass away;

title: Job 6:16
text: Which are black by reason of the ice, in which the snow hides itself.

title: Job 6:17
text: In the dry season, they vanish. When it is hot, they are consumed out of their place.

title: Job 6:18
text: The caravans that travel beside them turn aside. They go up into the waste, and perish.

title: Job 6:19
text: The caravans of Tema looked. The companies of Sheba waited for them.

title: Job 6:20
text: They were distressed because they were confident. They came there, and were confounded.

title: Job 6:21
text: For now you are nothing. You see a terror, and are afraid.

title: Job 6:22
text: Did I say, 'Give to me?' or, 'Offer a present for me from your substance?'

title: Job 6:23
text: or, 'Deliver me from the adversary's hand?' or, 'Redeem me from the hand of the oppressors?'

title: Job 6:24
text: "Teach me, and I will hold my peace. Cause me to understand wherein I have erred.

title: Job 6:25
text: How forcible are words of uprightness! But your reproof, what does it reprove?

title: Job 6:26
text: Do you intend to reprove words, since the speeches of one who is desperate are as wind?

title: Job 6:27
text: Yes, you would even cast lots for the fatherless, and make merchandise of your friend.

title: Job 6:28
text: Now therefore be pleased to look at me, for surely I shall not lie to your face.

title: Job 6:29
text: Please return. Let there be no injustice. Yes, return again. My cause is righteous.

title: Job 6:30
text: Is there injustice on my tongue? Can't my taste discern mischievous things?

title: Job 7:1
text: "Isn't a man forced to labor on earth? Aren't his days like the days of a hired hand?

title: Job 7:2
text: As a servant who earnestly desires the shadow, as a hireling who looks for his wages,

title: Job 7:3
text: so am I made to possess months of misery, wearisome nights are appointed to me.

title: Job 7:4
text: When I lie down, I say, 'When shall I arise, and the night be gone?' I toss and turn until the dawning of the day.

title: Job 7:5
text: My flesh is clothed with worms and clods of dust. My skin closes up, and breaks out afresh.

title: Job 7:6
text: My days are swifter than a weaver's shuttle, and are spent without hope.

title: Job 7:7
text: Oh remember that my life is a breath. My eye shall no more see good.

title: Job 7:8
text: The eye of him who sees me shall see me no more. Your eyes shall be on me, but I shall not be.

title: Job 7:9
text: As the cloud is consumed and vanishes away, so he who goes down to Sheol shall come up no more.

title: Job 7:10
text: He shall return no more to his house, neither shall his place know him any more.

title: Job 7:11
text: "Therefore I will not keep silent. I will speak in the anguish of my spirit. I will complain in the bitterness of my soul.

title: Job 7:12
text: Am I a sea, or a sea monster, that you put a guard over me?

title: Job 7:13
text: When I say, 'My bed shall comfort me. My couch shall ease my complaint;'

title: Job 7:14
text: then you scare me with dreams, and terrify me through visions:

title: Job 7:15
text: so that my soul chooses strangling, death rather than my bones.

title: Job 7:16
text: I loathe my life. I don't want to live forever. Leave me alone, for my days are but a breath.

title: Job 7:17
text: What is man, that you should magnify him, that you should set your mind on him,

title: Job 7:18
text: that you should visit him every morning, and test him every moment?

title: Job 7:19
text: How long will you not look away from me, nor leave me alone until I swallow down my spittle?

title: Job 7:20
text: If I have sinned, what do I do to you, you watcher of men? Why have you set me as a mark for you, so that I am a burden to myself?

title: Job 7:21
text: Why do you not pardon my disobedience, and take away my iniquity? For now shall I lie down in the dust. You will seek me diligently, but I shall not be."

title: Job 8:1
text: Then Bildad the Shuhite answered,

title: Job 8:2
text: "How long will you speak these things? Shall the words of your mouth be a mighty wind?

title: Job 8:3
text: Does God pervert justice? Or does the Almighty pervert righteousness?

title: Job 8:4
text: If your children have sinned against him, He has delivered them into the hand of their disobedience.

title: Job 8:5
text: If you want to seek God diligently, make your supplication to the Almighty.

title: Job 8:6
text: If you were pure and upright, surely now he would awaken for you, and make the habitation of your righteousness prosperous.

title: Job 8:7
text: Though your beginning was small, yet your latter end would greatly increase.

title: Job 8:8
text: "Please inquire of past generations. Find out about the learning of their fathers.

title: Job 8:9
text: (For we are but of yesterday, and know nothing, because our days on earth are a shadow.)

title: Job 8:10
text: Shall they not teach you, tell you, and utter words out of their heart?

title: Job 8:11
text: "Can the papyrus grow up without mire? Can the rushes grow without water?

title: Job 8:12
text: While it is yet in its greenness, not cut down, it withers before any other reed.

title: Job 8:13
text: So are the paths of all who forget God. The hope of the godless man shall perish,

title: Job 8:14
text: Whose confidence shall break apart, Whose trust is a spider's web.

title: Job 8:15
text: He shall lean on his house, but it shall not stand. He shall cling to it, but it shall not endure.

title: Job 8:16
text: He is green before the sun. His shoots go forth over his garden.

title: Job 8:17
text: His roots are wrapped around the rock pile. He sees the place of stones.

title: Job 8:18
text: If he is destroyed from his place, then it shall deny him, saying, 'I have not seen you.'

title: Job 8:19
text: Behold, this is the joy of his way: out of the earth, others shall spring.

title: Job 8:20
text: "Behold, God will not cast away a blameless man, neither will he uphold the evildoers.

title: Job 8:21
text: He will still fill your mouth with laughter, your lips with shouting.

title: Job 8:22
text: Those who hate you shall be clothed with shame. The tent of the wicked shall be no more."

title: Job 9:1
text: Then Job answered,

title: Job 9:2
text: "Truly I know that it is so, but how can man be just with God?

title: Job 9:3
text: If he is pleased to contend with him, he can't answer him one time in a thousand.

title: Job 9:4
text: God who is wise in heart, and mighty in strength: who has hardened himself against him, and prospered?

title: Job 9:5
text: He removes the mountains, and they don't know it, when he overturns them in his anger.

title: Job 9:6
text: He shakes the earth out of its place. Its pillars tremble.

title: Job 9:7
text: He commands the sun, and it doesn't rise, and seals up the stars.

title: Job 9:8
text: He alone stretches out the heavens, and treads on the waves of the sea.

title: Job 9:9
text: He makes the Bear, Orion, and the Pleiades, and the rooms of the south.

title: Job 9:10
text: He does great things past finding out; yes, marvelous things without number.

title: Job 9:11
text: Behold, he goes by me, and I don't see him. He passes on also, but I don't perceive him.

title: Job 9:12
text: Behold, he snatches away. Who can hinder him? Who will ask him, 'What are you doing?'

title: Job 9:13
text: "God will not withdraw his anger. The helpers of Rahab stoop under him.

title: Job 9:14
text: How much less shall I answer him, And choose my words to argue with him?

title: Job 9:15
text: Though I were righteous, yet I wouldn't answer him. I would make supplication to my judge.

title: Job 9:16
text: If I had called, and he had answered me, yet I wouldn't believe that he listened to my voice.

title: Job 9:17
text: For he breaks me with a storm, and multiplies my wounds without cause.

title: Job 9:18
text: He will not allow me to catch my breath, but fills me with bitterness.

title: Job 9:19
text: If it is a matter of strength, behold, he is mighty! If of justice, 'Who,' says he, 'will summon me?'

title: Job 9:20
text: Though I am righteous, my own mouth shall condemn me. Though I am blameless, it shall prove me perverse.

title: Job 9:21
text: I am blameless. I don't respect myself. I despise my life.

title: Job 9:22
text: "It is all the same. Therefore I say he destroys the blameless and the wicked.

title: Job 9:23
text: If the scourge kills suddenly, he will mock at the trial of the innocent.

title: Job 9:24
text: The earth is given into the hand of the wicked. He covers the faces of its judges. If not he, then who is it?

title: Job 9:25
text: "Now my days are swifter than a runner. They flee away, they see no good,

title: Job 9:26
text: They have passed away as the swift ships, as the eagle that swoops on the prey.

title: Job 9:27
text: If I say, 'I will forget my complaint, I will put off my sad face, and cheer up;'

title: Job 9:28
text: I am afraid of all my sorrows, I know that you will not hold me innocent.

title: Job 9:29
text: I shall be condemned. Why then do I labor in vain?

title: Job 9:30
text: If I wash myself with snow, and cleanse my hands with lye,

title: Job 9:31
text: yet you will plunge me in the ditch. My own clothes shall abhor me.

title: Job 9:32
text: For he is not a man, as I am, that I should answer him, that we should come together in judgment.

title: Job 9:33
text: There is no umpire between us, that might lay his hand on us both.

title: Job 9:34
text: Let him take his rod away from me. Let his terror not make me afraid;

title: Job 9:35
text: then I would speak, and not fear him, for I am not so in myself.

title: Job 10:1
text: "My soul is weary of my life. I will give free course to my complaint. I will speak in the bitterness of my soul.

title: Job 10:2
text: I will tell God, 'Do not condemn me. Show me why you contend with me.

title: Job 10:3
text: Is it good to you that you should oppress, that you should despise the work of your hands, and smile on the counsel of the wicked?

title: Job 10:4
text: Do you have eyes of flesh? Or do you see as man sees?

title: Job 10:5
text: Are your days as the days of mortals, or your years as man's years,

title: Job 10:6
text: that you inquire after my iniquity, and search after my sin?

title: Job 10:7
text: Although you know that I am not wicked, there is no one who can deliver out of your hand.

title: Job 10:8
text: "'Your hands have framed me and fashioned me altogether, yet you destroy me.

title: Job 10:9
text: Remember, I beg you, that you have fashioned me as clay. Will you bring me into dust again?

title: Job 10:10
text: Haven't you poured me out like milk, and curdled me like cheese?

title: Job 10:11
text: You have clothed me with skin and flesh, and knit me together with bones and sinews.

title: Job 10:12
text: You have granted me life and loving kindness. Your visitation has preserved my spirit.

title: Job 10:13
text: Yet you hid these things in your heart. I know that this is with you:

title: Job 10:14
text: if I sin, then you mark me. You will not acquit me from my iniquity.

title: Job 10:15
text: If I am wicked, woe to me. If I am righteous, I still shall not lift up my head, being filled with disgrace, and conscious of my affliction.

title: Job 10:16
text: If my head is held high, you hunt me like a lion. Again you show yourself powerful to me.

title: Job 10:17
text: You renew your witnesses against me, and increase your indignation on me. Changes and warfare are with me.

title: Job 10:18
text: "'Why, then, have you brought me forth out of the womb? I wish I had given up the spirit, and no eye had seen me.

title: Job 10:19
text: I should have been as though I had not been. I should have been carried from the womb to the grave.

title: Job 10:20
text: Aren't my days few? Cease then. Leave me alone, that I may find a little comfort,

title: Job 10:21
text: before I go where I shall not return from, to the land of darkness and of the shadow of death;

title: Job 10:22
text: the land dark as midnight, of the shadow of death, without any order, where the light is as midnight.'"

title: Job 11:1
text: Then Zophar, the Naamathite, answered,

title: Job 11:2
text: "Shouldn't the multitude of words be answered? Should a man full of talk be justified?

title: Job 11:3
text: Should your boastings make men hold their peace? When you mock, shall no man make you ashamed?

title: Job 11:4
text: For you say, 'My doctrine is pure. I am clean in your eyes.'

title: Job 11:5
text: But oh that God would speak, and open his lips against you,

title: Job 11:6
text: that he would show you the secrets of wisdom! For true wisdom has two sides. Know therefore that God exacts of you less than your iniquity deserves.

title: Job 11:7
text: "Can you fathom the mystery of God? Or can you probe the limits of the Almighty?

title: Job 11:8
text: They are high as heaven. What can you do? They are deeper than Sheol. What can you know?

title: Job 11:9
text: Its measure is longer than the earth, and broader than the sea.

title: Job 11:10
text: If he passes by, or confines, or convenes a court, then who can oppose him?

title: Job 11:11
text: For he knows false men. He sees iniquity also, even though he doesn't consider it.

title: Job 11:12
text: An empty-headed man becomes wise when a man is born as a wild donkey's colt.

title: Job 11:13
text: "If you set your heart aright, stretch out your hands toward him.

title: Job 11:14
text: If iniquity is in your hand, put it far away. Don't let unrighteousness dwell in your tents.

title: Job 11:15
text: Surely then you shall lift up your face without spot; Yes, you shall be steadfast, and shall not fear:

title: Job 11:16
text: for you shall forget your misery. You shall remember it as waters that are passed away.

title: Job 11:17
text: Life shall be clearer than the noonday. Though there is darkness, it shall be as the morning.

title: Job 11:18
text: You shall be secure, because there is hope. Yes, you shall search, and shall take your rest in safety.

title: Job 11:19
text: Also you shall lie down, and none shall make you afraid. Yes, many shall court your favor.

title: Job 11:20
text: But the eyes of the wicked shall fail. They shall have no way to flee. Their hope shall be the giving up of the spirit."

title: Job 12:1
text: Then Job answered,

title: Job 12:2
text: "No doubt, but you are the people, and wisdom shall die with you.

title: Job 12:3
text: But I have understanding as well as you; I am not inferior to you. Yes, who doesn't know such things as these?

title: Job 12:4
text: I am like one who is a joke to his neighbor, I, who called on God, and he answered. The just, the blameless man is a joke.

title: Job 12:5
text: In the thought of him who is at ease there is contempt for misfortune. It is ready for them whose foot slips.

title: Job 12:6
text: The tents of robbers prosper. Those who provoke God are secure, who carry their God in their hands.

title: Job 12:7
text: "But ask the animals, now, and they shall teach you; the birds of the sky, and they shall tell you.

title: Job 12:8
text: Or speak to the earth, and it shall teach you. The fish of the sea shall declare to you.

title: Job 12:9
text: Who doesn't know that in all these, the hand of Yahweh has done this,

title: Job 12:10
text: in whose hand is the life of every living thing, and the breath of all mankind?

title: Job 12:11
text: Doesn't the ear try words, even as the palate tastes its food?

title: Job 12:12
text: With aged men is wisdom, in length of days understanding.

title: Job 12:13
text: "With God is wisdom and might. He has counsel and understanding.

title: Job 12:14
text: Behold, he breaks down, and it can't be built again. He imprisons a man, and there can be no release.

title: Job 12:15
text: Behold, he withholds the waters, and they dry up. Again, he sends them out, and they overturn the earth.

title: Job 12:16
text: With him is strength and wisdom. The deceived and the deceiver are his.

title: Job 12:17
text: He leads counselors away stripped. He makes judges fools.

title: Job 12:18
text: He loosens the bond of kings. He binds their waist with a belt.

title: Job 12:19
text: He leads priests away stripped, and overthrows the mighty.

title: Job 12:20
text: He removes the speech of those who are trusted, and takes away the understanding of the elders.

title: Job 12:21
text: He pours contempt on princes, and loosens the belt of the strong.

title: Job 12:22
text: He uncovers deep things out of darkness, and brings out to light the shadow of death.

title: Job 12:23
text: He increases the nations, and he destroys them. He enlarges the nations, and he leads them captive.

title: Job 12:24
text: He takes away understanding from the chiefs of the people of the earth, and causes them to wander in a wilderness where there is no way.

title: Job 12:25
text: They grope in the dark without light. He makes them stagger like a drunken man.

title: Job 13:1
text: "Behold, my eye has seen all this. My ear has heard and understood it.

title: Job 13:2
text: What you know, I know also. I am not inferior to you.

title: Job 13:3
text: "Surely I would speak to the Almighty. I desire to reason with God.

title: Job 13:4
text: But you are forgers of lies. You are all physicians of no value.

title: Job 13:5
text: Oh that you would be completely silent! Then you would be wise.

title: Job 13:6
text: Hear now my reasoning. Listen to the pleadings of my lips.

title: Job 13:7
text: Will you speak unrighteously for God, and talk deceitfully for him?

title: Job 13:8
text: Will you show partiality to him? Will you contend for God?

title: Job 13:9
text: Is it good that he should search you out? Or as one deceives a man, will you deceive him?

title: Job 13:10
text: He will surely reprove you if you secretly show partiality.

title: Job 13:11
text: Shall not his majesty make you afraid, And his dread fall on you?

title: Job 13:12
text: Your memorable sayings are proverbs of ashes, Your defenses are defenses of clay.

title: Job 13:13
text: "Be silent, leave me alone, that I may speak. Let come on me what will.

title: Job 13:14
text: Why should I take my flesh in my teeth, and put my life in my hand?

title: Job 13:15
text: Behold, he will kill me. I have no hope. Nevertheless, I will maintain my ways before him.

title: Job 13:16
text: This also shall be my salvation, that a godless man shall not come before him.

title: Job 13:17
text: Hear diligently my speech. Let my declaration be in your ears.

title: Job 13:18
text: See now, I have set my cause in order. I know that I am righteous.

title: Job 13:19
text: Who is he who will contend with me? For then would I hold my peace and give up the spirit.

title: Job 13:20
text: "Only don't do two things to me; then I will not hide myself from your face:

title: Job 13:21
text: withdraw your hand far from me; and don't let your terror make me afraid.

title: Job 13:22
text: Then call, and I will answer; or let me speak, and you answer me.

title: Job 13:23
text: How many are my iniquities and sins? Make me know my disobedience and my sin.

title: Job 13:24
text: Why hide you your face, and hold me for your enemy?

title: Job 13:25
text: Will you harass a driven leaf? Will you pursue the dry stubble?

title: Job 13:26
text: For you write bitter things against me, and make me inherit the iniquities of my youth:

title: Job 13:27
text: You also put my feet in the stocks, and mark all my paths. You set a bound to the soles of my feet,

title: Job 13:28
text: though I am decaying like a rotten thing, like a garment that is moth-eaten.

title: Job 14:1
text: "Man, who is born of a woman, is of few days, and full of trouble.

title: Job 14:2
text: He comes forth like a flower, and is cut down. He also flees like a shadow, and doesn't continue.

title: Job 14:3
text: Do you open your eyes on such a one, and bring me into judgment with you?

title: Job 14:4
text: Who can bring a clean thing out of an unclean? Not one.

title: Job 14:5
text: Seeing his days are determined, the number of his months is with you, and you have appointed his bounds that he can't pass;

title: Job 14:6
text: Look away from him, that he may rest, until he shall accomplish, as a hireling, his day.

title: Job 14:7
text: "For there is hope for a tree, If it is cut down, that it will sprout again, that the tender branch of it will not cease.

title: Job 14:8
text: Though its root grows old in the earth, and its stock dies in the ground,

title: Job 14:9
text: yet through the scent of water it will bud, and put forth boughs like a plant.

title: Job 14:10
text: But man dies, and is laid low. Yes, man gives up the spirit, and where is he?

title: Job 14:11
text: As the waters fail from the sea, and the river wastes and dries up,

title: Job 14:12
text: so man lies down and doesn't rise. Until the heavens are no more, they shall not awake, nor be roused out of their sleep.

title: Job 14:13
text: "Oh that you would hide me in Sheol, that you would keep me secret, until your wrath is past, that you would appoint me a set time, and remember me!

title: Job 14:14
text: If a man dies, shall he live again? All the days of my warfare would I wait, until my release should come.

title: Job 14:15
text: You would call, and I would answer you. You would have a desire to the work of your hands.

title: Job 14:16
text: But now you number my steps. Don't you watch over my sin?

title: Job 14:17
text: My disobedience is sealed up in a bag. You fasten up my iniquity.

title: Job 14:18
text: "But the mountain falling comes to nothing. The rock is removed out of its place;

title: Job 14:19
text: The waters wear the stones. The torrents of it wash away the dust of the earth. So you destroy the hope of man.

title: Job 14:20
text: You forever prevail against him, and he departs. You change his face, and send him away.

title: Job 14:21
text: His sons come to honor, and he doesn't know it. They are brought low, but he doesn't perceive it of them.

title: Job 14:22
text: But his flesh on him has pain, and his soul within him mourns."

title: Job 15:1
text: Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered,

title: Job 15:2
text: "Should a wise man answer with vain knowledge, and fill himself with the east wind?

title: Job 15:3
text: Should he reason with unprofitable talk, or with speeches with which he can do no good?

title: Job 15:4
text: Yes, you do away with fear, and hinder devotion before God.

title: Job 15:5
text: For your iniquity teaches your mouth, and you choose the language of the crafty.

title: Job 15:6
text: Your own mouth condemns you, and not I. Yes, your own lips testify against you.

title: Job 15:7
text: "Are you the first man who was born? Or were you brought forth before the hills?

title: Job 15:8
text: Have you heard the secret counsel of God? Do you limit wisdom to yourself?

title: Job 15:9
text: What do you know, that we don't know? What do you understand, which is not in us?

title: Job 15:10
text: With us are both the gray-headed and the very aged men, much elder than your father.

title: Job 15:11
text: Are the consolations of God too small for you, even the word that is gentle toward you?

title: Job 15:12
text: Why does your heart carry you away? Why do your eyes flash,

title: Job 15:13
text: That you turn your spirit against God, and let such words go out of your mouth?

title: Job 15:14
text: What is man, that he should be clean? What is he who is born of a woman, that he should be righteous?

title: Job 15:15
text: Behold, he puts no trust in his holy ones. Yes, the heavens are not clean in his sight;

title: Job 15:16
text: how much less one who is abominable and corrupt, a man who drinks iniquity like water!

title: Job 15:17
text: "I will show you, listen to me; that which I have seen I will declare:

title: Job 15:18
text: (Which wise men have told by their fathers, and have not hidden it;

title: Job 15:19
text: to whom alone the land was given, and no stranger passed among them):

title: Job 15:20
text: the wicked man writhes in pain all his days, even the number of years that are laid up for the oppressor.

title: Job 15:21
text: A sound of terrors is in his ears. In prosperity the destroyer shall come on him.

title: Job 15:22
text: He doesn't believe that he shall return out of darkness. He is waited for by the sword.

title: Job 15:23
text: He wanders abroad for bread, saying, 'Where is it?' He knows that the day of darkness is ready at his hand.

title: Job 15:24
text: Distress and anguish make him afraid. They prevail against him, as a king ready to the battle.

title: Job 15:25
text: Because he has stretched out his hand against God, and behaves himself proudly against the Almighty;

title: Job 15:26
text: he runs at him with a stiff neck, with the thick shields of his bucklers;

title: Job 15:27
text: because he has covered his face with his fatness, and gathered fat on his thighs.

title: Job 15:28
text: He has lived in desolate cities, in houses which no one inhabited, which were ready to become heaps.

title: Job 15:29
text: He shall not be rich, neither shall his substance continue, neither shall their possessions be extended on the earth.

title: Job 15:30
text: He shall not depart out of darkness. The flame shall dry up his branches. By the breath of God's mouth shall he go away.

title: Job 15:31
text: Let him not trust in emptiness, deceiving himself; for emptiness shall be his reward.

title: Job 15:32
text: It shall be accomplished before his time. His branch shall not be green.

title: Job 15:33
text: He shall shake off his unripe grape as the vine, and shall cast off his flower as the olive tree.

title: Job 15:34
text: For the company of the godless shall be barren, and fire shall consume the tents of bribery.

title: Job 15:35
text: They conceive mischief, and bring forth iniquity. Their heart prepares deceit."

title: Job 16:1
text: Then Job answered,

title: Job 16:2
text: "I have heard many such things. You are all miserable comforters!

title: Job 16:3
text: Shall vain words have an end? Or what provokes you that you answer?

title: Job 16:4
text: I also could speak as you do. If your soul were in my soul's place, I could join words together against you, and shake my head at you,

title: Job 16:5
text: but I would strengthen you with my mouth. The solace of my lips would relieve you.

title: Job 16:6
text: "Though I speak, my grief is not subsided. Though I forbear, what am I eased?

title: Job 16:7
text: But now, God, you have surely worn me out. You have made desolate all my company.

title: Job 16:8
text: You have shriveled me up. This is a witness against me. My leanness rises up against me. It testifies to my face.

title: Job 16:9
text: He has torn me in his wrath, and persecuted me. He has gnashed on me with his teeth. My adversary sharpens his eyes on me.

title: Job 16:10
text: They have gaped on me with their mouth. They have struck me on the cheek reproachfully. They gather themselves together against me.

title: Job 16:11
text: God delivers me to the ungodly, and casts me into the hands of the wicked.

title: Job 16:12
text: I was at ease, and he broke me apart. Yes, he has taken me by the neck, and dashed me to pieces. He has also set me up for his target.

title: Job 16:13
text: His archers surround me. He splits my kidneys apart, and does not spare. He pours out my gall on the ground.

title: Job 16:14
text: He breaks me with breach on breach. He runs on me like a giant.

title: Job 16:15
text: I have sewed sackcloth on my skin, and have thrust my horn in the dust.

title: Job 16:16
text: My face is red with weeping. Deep darkness is on my eyelids.

title: Job 16:17
text: Although there is no violence in my hands, and my prayer is pure.

title: Job 16:18
text: "Earth, don't cover my blood. Let my cry have no place to rest.

title: Job 16:19
text: Even now, behold, my witness is in heaven. He who vouches for me is on high.

title: Job 16:20
text: My friends scoff at me. My eyes pour out tears to God,

title: Job 16:21
text: that he would maintain the right of a man with God, of a son of man with his neighbor!

title: Job 16:22
text: For when a few years are come, I shall go the way of no return.

title: Job 17:1
text: "My spirit is consumed. My days are extinct, And the grave is ready for me.

title: Job 17:2
text: Surely there are mockers with me. My eye dwells on their provocation.

title: Job 17:3
text: "Now give a pledge, be collateral for me with yourself. Who is there who will strike hands with me?

title: Job 17:4
text: For you have hidden their heart from understanding, Therefore you shall not exalt them.

title: Job 17:5
text: He who denounces his friends for a prey, Even the eyes of his children shall fail.

title: Job 17:6
text: "But he has made me a byword of the people. They spit in my face.

title: Job 17:7
text: My eye also is dim by reason of sorrow. All my members are as a shadow.

title: Job 17:8
text: Upright men shall be astonished at this. The innocent shall stir up himself against the godless.

title: Job 17:9
text: Yet shall the righteous hold on his way. He who has clean hands shall grow stronger and stronger.

title: Job 17:10
text: But as for you all, come on now again; I shall not find a wise man among you.

title: Job 17:11
text: My days are past, my plans are broken off, as are the thoughts of my heart.

title: Job 17:12
text: They change the night into day, saying 'The light is near' in the presence of darkness.

title: Job 17:13
text: If I look for Sheol as my house, if I have spread my couch in the darkness,

title: Job 17:14
text: If I have said to corruption, 'You are my father;' to the worm, 'My mother,' and 'my sister;'

title: Job 17:15
text: where then is my hope? as for my hope, who shall see it?

title: Job 17:16
text: Shall it go down with me to the gates of Sheol, or descend together into the dust?"

title: Job 18:1
text: Then Bildad the Shuhite answered,

title: Job 18:2
text: "How long will you hunt for words? Consider, and afterwards we will speak.

title: Job 18:3
text: Why are we counted as animals, which have become unclean in your sight?

title: Job 18:4
text: You who tear yourself in your anger, shall the earth be forsaken for you? Or shall the rock be removed out of its place?

title: Job 18:5
text: "Yes, the light of the wicked shall be put out, The spark of his fire shall not shine.

title: Job 18:6
text: The light shall be dark in his tent. His lamp above him shall be put out.

title: Job 18:7
text: The steps of his strength shall be shortened. His own counsel shall cast him down.

title: Job 18:8
text: For he is cast into a net by his own feet, and he wanders into its mesh.

title: Job 18:9
text: A snare will take him by the heel. A trap will catch him.

title: Job 18:10
text: A noose is hidden for him in the ground, a trap for him in the way.

title: Job 18:11
text: Terrors shall make him afraid on every side, and shall chase him at his heels.

title: Job 18:12
text: His strength shall be famished. Calamity shall be ready at his side.

title: Job 18:13
text: The members of his body shall be devoured. The firstborn of death shall devour his members.

title: Job 18:14
text: He shall be rooted out of his tent where he trusts. He shall be brought to the king of terrors.

title: Job 18:15
text: There shall dwell in his tent that which is none of his. Sulfur shall be scattered on his habitation.

title: Job 18:16
text: His roots shall be dried up beneath. Above shall his branch be cut off.

title: Job 18:17
text: His memory shall perish from the earth. He shall have no name in the street.

title: Job 18:18
text: He shall be driven from light into darkness, and chased out of the world.

title: Job 18:19
text: He shall have neither son nor grandson among his people, nor any remaining where he lived.

title: Job 18:20
text: Those who come after shall be astonished at his day, as those who went before were frightened.

title: Job 18:21
text: Surely such are the dwellings of the unrighteous. This is the place of him who doesn't know God."

title: Job 19:1
text: Then Job answered,

title: Job 19:2
text: "How long will you torment me, and crush me with words?

title: Job 19:3
text: You have reproached me ten times. You aren't ashamed that you attack me.

title: Job 19:4
text: If it is true that I have erred, my error remains with myself.

title: Job 19:5
text: If indeed you will magnify yourselves against me, and plead against me my reproach;

title: Job 19:6
text: know now that God has subverted me, and has surrounded me with his net.

title: Job 19:7
text: "Behold, I cry out of wrong, but I am not heard. I cry for help, but there is no justice.

title: Job 19:8
text: He has walled up my way so that I can't pass, and has set darkness in my paths.

title: Job 19:9
text: He has stripped me of my glory, and taken the crown from my head.

title: Job 19:10
text: He has broken me down on every side, and I am gone. My hope he has plucked up like a tree.

title: Job 19:11
text: He has also kindled his wrath against me. He counts me among his adversaries.

title: Job 19:12
text: His troops come on together, build a siege ramp against me, and encamp around my tent.

title: Job 19:13
text: "He has put my brothers far from me. My acquaintances are wholly estranged from me.

title: Job 19:14
text: My relatives have gone away. My familiar friends have forgotten me.

title: Job 19:15
text: Those who dwell in my house, and my maids, count me for a stranger. I am an alien in their sight.

title: Job 19:16
text: I call to my servant, and he gives me no answer. I beg him with my mouth.

title: Job 19:17
text: My breath is offensive to my wife. I am loathsome to the children of my own mother.

title: Job 19:18
text: Even young children despise me. If I arise, they speak against me.

title: Job 19:19
text: All my familiar friends abhor me. They whom I loved have turned against me.

title: Job 19:20
text: My bones stick to my skin and to my flesh. I have escaped by the skin of my teeth.

title: Job 19:21
text: "Have pity on me, have pity on me, you my friends; for the hand of God has touched me.

title: Job 19:22
text: Why do you persecute me as God, and are not satisfied with my flesh?

title: Job 19:23
text: "Oh that my words were now written! Oh that they were inscribed in a book!

title: Job 19:24
text: That with an iron pen and lead they were engraved in the rock forever!

title: Job 19:25
text: But as for me, I know that my Redeemer lives. In the end, he will stand upon the earth.

title: Job 19:26
text: After my skin is destroyed, then in my flesh shall I see God,

title: Job 19:27
text: Whom I, even I, shall see on my side. My eyes shall see, and not as a stranger. "My heart is consumed within me.

title: Job 19:28
text: If you say, 'How we will persecute him!' because the root of the matter is found in me,

title: Job 19:29
text: be afraid of the sword, for wrath brings the punishments of the sword, that you may know there is a judgment."

title: Job 20:1
text: Then Zophar the Naamathite answered,

title: Job 20:2
text: "Therefore do my thoughts give answer to me, even by reason of my haste that is in me.

title: Job 20:3
text: I have heard the reproof which puts me to shame. The spirit of my understanding answers me.

title: Job 20:4
text: Don't you know this from old time, since man was placed on earth,

title: Job 20:5
text: that the triumphing of the wicked is short, the joy of the godless but for a moment?

title: Job 20:6
text: Though his height mount up to the heavens, and his head reach to the clouds,

title: Job 20:7
text: yet he shall perish forever like his own dung. Those who have seen him shall say, 'Where is he?'

title: Job 20:8
text: He shall fly away as a dream, and shall not be found. Yes, he shall be chased away like a vision of the night.

title: Job 20:9
text: The eye which saw him shall see him no more, neither shall his place any more see him.

title: Job 20:10
text: His children shall seek the favor of the poor. His hands shall give back his wealth.

title: Job 20:11
text: His bones are full of his youth, but youth shall lie down with him in the dust.

title: Job 20:12
text: "Though wickedness is sweet in his mouth, though he hide it under his tongue,

title: Job 20:13
text: though he spare it, and will not let it go, but keep it still within his mouth;

title: Job 20:14
text: yet his food in his bowels is turned. It is cobra venom within him.

title: Job 20:15
text: He has swallowed down riches, and he shall vomit them up again. God will cast them out of his belly.

title: Job 20:16
text: He shall suck cobra venom. The viper's tongue shall kill him.

title: Job 20:17
text: He shall not look at the rivers, the flowing streams of honey and butter.

title: Job 20:18
text: That for which he labored he shall restore, and shall not swallow it down. According to the substance that he has gotten, he shall not rejoice.

title: Job 20:19
text: For he has oppressed and forsaken the poor. He has violently taken away a house, and he shall not build it up.

title: Job 20:20
text: "Because he knew no quietness within him, he shall not save anything of that in which he delights.

title: Job 20:21
text: There was nothing left that he didn't devour, therefore his prosperity shall not endure.

title: Job 20:22
text: In the fullness of his sufficiency, distress shall overtake him. The hand of everyone who is in misery shall come on him.

title: Job 20:23
text: When he is about to fill his belly, God will cast the fierceness of his wrath on him. It will rain on him while he is eating.

title: Job 20:24
text: He shall flee from the iron weapon. The bronze arrow shall strike him through.

title: Job 20:25
text: He draws it forth, and it comes out of his body. Yes, the glittering point comes out of his liver. Terrors are on him.

title: Job 20:26
text: All darkness is laid up for his treasures. An unfanned fire shall devour him. It shall consume that which is left in his tent.

title: Job 20:27
text: The heavens shall reveal his iniquity. The earth shall rise up against him.

title: Job 20:28
text: The increase of his house shall depart. They shall rush away in the day of his wrath.

title: Job 20:29
text: This is the portion of a wicked man from God, the heritage appointed to him by God."

title: Job 21:1
text: Then Job answered,

title: Job 21:2
text: "Listen diligently to my speech. Let this be your consolation.

title: Job 21:3
text: Allow me, and I also will speak; After I have spoken, mock on.

title: Job 21:4
text: As for me, is my complaint to man? Why shouldn't I be impatient?

title: Job 21:5
text: Look at me, and be astonished. Lay your hand on your mouth.

title: Job 21:6
text: When I remember, I am troubled. Horror takes hold of my flesh.

title: Job 21:7
text: "Why do the wicked live, become old, yes, and grow mighty in power?

title: Job 21:8
text: Their child is established with them in their sight, their offspring before their eyes.

title: Job 21:9
text: Their houses are safe from fear, neither is the rod of God upon them.

title: Job 21:10
text: Their bulls breed without fail. Their cows calve, and don't miscarry.

title: Job 21:11
text: They send forth their little ones like a flock. Their children dance.

title: Job 21:12
text: They sing to the tambourine and harp, and rejoice at the sound of the pipe.

title: Job 21:13
text: They spend their days in prosperity. In an instant they go down to Sheol.

title: Job 21:14
text: They tell God, 'Depart from us, for we don't want to know about your ways.

title: Job 21:15
text: What is the Almighty, that we should serve him? What profit should we have, if we pray to him?'

title: Job 21:16
text: Behold, their prosperity is not in their hand. The counsel of the wicked is far from me.

title: Job 21:17
text: "How often is it that the lamp of the wicked is put out, that their calamity comes on them, that God distributes sorrows in his anger?

title: Job 21:18
text: How often is it that they are as stubble before the wind, as chaff that the storm carries away?

title: Job 21:19
text: You say, 'God lays up his iniquity for his children.' Let him recompense it to himself, that he may know it.

title: Job 21:20
text: Let his own eyes see his destruction. Let him drink of the wrath of the Almighty.

title: Job 21:21
text: For what does he care for his house after him, when the number of his months is cut off?

title: Job 21:22
text: "Shall any teach God knowledge, since he judges those who are high?

title: Job 21:23
text: One dies in his full strength, being wholly at ease and quiet.

title: Job 21:24
text: His pails are full of milk. The marrow of his bones is moistened.

title: Job 21:25
text: Another dies in bitterness of soul, and never tastes of good.

title: Job 21:26
text: They lie down alike in the dust. The worm covers them.

title: Job 21:27
text: "Behold, I know your thoughts, the devices with which you would wrong me.

title: Job 21:28
text: For you say, 'Where is the house of the prince? Where is the tent in which the wicked lived?'

title: Job 21:29
text: Haven't you asked wayfaring men? Don't you know their evidences,

title: Job 21:30
text: that the evil man is reserved to the day of calamity, That they are led forth to the day of wrath?

title: Job 21:31
text: Who shall declare his way to his face? Who shall repay him what he has done?

title: Job 21:32
text: Yet he will be borne to the grave. Men shall keep watch over the tomb.

title: Job 21:33
text: The clods of the valley shall be sweet to him. All men shall draw after him, as there were innumerable before him.

title: Job 21:34
text: So how can you comfort me with nonsense, because in your answers there remains only falsehood?"

title: Job 22:1
text: Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered,

title: Job 22:2
text: "Can a man be profitable to God? Surely he who is wise is profitable to himself.

title: Job 22:3
text: Is it any pleasure to the Almighty, that you are righteous? Or does it benefit him, that you make your ways perfect?

title: Job 22:4
text: Is it for your piety that he reproves you, that he enters with you into judgment?

title: Job 22:5
text: Isn't your wickedness great? Neither is there any end to your iniquities.

title: Job 22:6
text: For you have taken pledges from your brother for nothing, and stripped the naked of their clothing.

title: Job 22:7
text: You haven't given water to the weary to drink, and you have withheld bread from the hungry.

title: Job 22:8
text: But as for the mighty man, he had the earth. The honorable man, he lived in it.

title: Job 22:9
text: You have sent widows away empty, and the arms of the fatherless have been broken.

title: Job 22:10
text: Therefore snares are around you. Sudden fear troubles you,

title: Job 22:11
text: or darkness, so that you can not see, and floods of waters cover you.

title: Job 22:12
text: "Isn't God in the heights of heaven? See the height of the stars, how high they are!

title: Job 22:13
text: You say, 'What does God know? Can he judge through the thick darkness?

title: Job 22:14
